nodes.label: Zeroized crypto metadata and future current-fact one-time writer binding
nodes.community_name: Rust implementation progress on codex/rust-platform; epic #672 and 55 issues remain the full goal
nodes.norm_label: zeroized crypto metadata and future current-fact one-time writer binding
nodes.rationale: Signer, bearer and verified metadata omit Debug/Clone/Serde; owned key, token and decoded claims are zeroizing where supported, without universal parser/library/allocator copies or whole-operation constant-time claims. Verified metadata is a crypto observation, never an authenticated principal. It binds to signer workspace and key and exposes email, nonce, time and a token digest for the future admitted writer. Email here is a bounded lowercase ASCII coordinate, not a user lookup, deliverability decision or the storage layer's complete email policy. Future use must validate the canonical current user/email and native issuance context under a writer, enforce single consumption/revocation/history and distinguish known/unknown commit before redirect or mail. Signature validity alone must never mark an email verified.

nodes.label: Native email-token crypto without verified-user or persistence authority
nodes.community_name: Rust implementation progress on codex/rust-platform; epic #672 and 55 issues remain the full goal
nodes.norm_label: native email-token crypto without verified-user or persistence authority
nodes.rationale: The configured source signs verification JWTs with HS256 using the original active secret string, lowercased email, integer issued-at and one-hour expiry. It does not use the retained MFA encryption keyring, store a token context or prevent replay. This prerequisite adds native crypto only: no HTTP, database issuance/consumption, mail, verified user, membership, MFA or session authority. The full email-verification flow remains the next required work; the Rust epic is unchanged.

nodes.label: Source/jose crypto acceptance and pending complete verification flow
nodes.community_name: Rust implementation progress on codex/rust-platform; epic #672 and 55 issues remain the full goal
nodes.norm_label: source/jose crypto acceptance and pending complete verification flow
nodes.rationale: Acceptance uses native strict-boundary tests plus installed jose/source JWT oracles in both directions, HMAC mutation controls, same-second random issuance, exact expiry/future/lifetime, key/workspace/purpose separation and forbidden legacy/change-email envelopes. Existing native identity tests remain unchanged. Scoped GDD is structural readiness for this crypto primitive only. HTTP callbacks, persistent one-time context, actual mail, issuer/recipient policy, current-user transaction, deployments and full R04/R41/R42 acceptance are not qualified.

nodes.label: Strict source-readable HS256 native purpose/workspace/random nonce envelope
nodes.community_name: Rust implementation progress on codex/rust-platform; epic #672 and 55 issues remain the full goal
nodes.norm_label: strict source-readable hs256 native purpose/workspace/random nonce envelope
nodes.rationale: Native tokens retain source-readable HS256/email/iat/exp and add mandatory purpose=rentemester-email-verification-v1, trusted workspace and256-bit random jti. Native verification accepts only that envelope under the configured current key/workspace. No legacy stateless token adoption, rotation fallback, email change updateTo/requestType, generic JWT or other purpose is accepted. Each issuance samples a trusted Clock once; iat=floor(ms/1000), exp=iat+3600. Verification samples once and requires iat<=now<exp with exact one-hour lifetime and finite calendar bounds. It verifies the raw compact signing input with constant-time HMAC comparison before accepting claims, rejects padding/noncanonical base64url/extra segments/duplicate or unknown JSON fields, wrong types, oversized data, algorithm/header confusion and malformed nonce. Errors are fixed AuthError variants, never bearer/claim/parser text.

nodes.label: Writer-time freshness and mandatory legacy verification-route closure
nodes.community_name: Rust implementation progress on codex/rust-platform; epic #672 and 55 issues remain the full goal
nodes.norm_label: writer-time freshness and mandatory legacy verification-route closure
nodes.rationale: Integration review requires fresh time validation under writer admission: accepts(proof) binds only workspace/key and cannot certify later freshness. The legacy /verify-email handler accepts the native envelope but ignores its extra context claims. It must not remain an authoritative verification writer alongside native routes; wire/crypto interoperability is not safe dual-endpoint qualification. Native one-time context and legacy-route closure must ship together before enabling actual verification.

nodes.label: Access policy independent corpus and pending authentication/fencing
nodes.community_name: Rust implementation progress on codex/rust-platform; epic #672 and 55 issues remain the full goal
nodes.norm_label: access policy independent corpus and pending authentication/fencing
nodes.rationale: The access-policy/ contract and scoped readiness precede the implementation; four native tests and 2485 corpus/environment checks pass, independently repeated. All 2484 fixed independent cases also run actual unchanged TypeScript control-store authorization on synthetic current stores; every role-table result is compared directly. The 505 explicit differences retain upstream session/credential preconditions and stricter cross-scope binding rather than claiming legacy core alone verified them. Native evaluations are repeated over immutable facts in two environments; legacy control images/total_changes, manifest and unopened company sentinel remain unchanged around each read. The new crate needs only the existing serde dependency; domain/application guards reject SQL/OS dependencies. This is a shared policy foundation, not authentication, stable persisted identity, source event collection, concurrent revocation fencing, last-owner mutation logic or full R04/R13 completion. Actual authenticated write orchestration, other domains/interfaces/distribution and cutover remain outstanding.

nodes.label: Locked code-pool CAS and atomic session/source interoperability
nodes.community_name: Rust implementation progress on codex/rust-platform; epic #672 and 55 issues remain the full goal
nodes.norm_label: locked code-pool cas and atomic session/source interoperability
nodes.rationale: Successful recovery uses the current encrypted pool under the writer lock and an exact old-ciphertext compare-and-set. One code removal, account reset, challenge consumption, fresh twelve-hour session and accepted recovery audit commit together; cookies return only after known commit. TOTP replay records remain untouched. The backup-login/ contract/readiness and evidence cover actual configured Better Auth pool generation, decryption/session readers and HTTP backup-code consumption on a separate synthetic copy, WAL/DELETE different-challenge races, cross-method failure budgets, malformed pools, late SQL rollback and real commit-busy. Historical-key consumption rewrites with the configured current key; retired keys do not silently fall back.

nodes.label: Atomic setup confirmation and one-time committed backup disclosure
nodes.community_name: Rust implementation progress on codex/rust-platform; epic #672 and 55 issues remain the full goal
nodes.norm_label: atomic setup confirmation and one-time committed backup disclosure
nodes.rationale: Confirmation accepts only the enrollment namespace and current disabled-user/unverified-factor state. It shares the verified TOTP primitive, strict current control admission, challenge/account budgets and transaction machinery with login, while enrolled TOTP/backup login cannot finish setup. Successful confirmation marks the factor/user enabled, lets the existing trigger revoke every prior session, records the accepted TOTP counter, burns the ceremony and creates a fresh twelve-hour session. Its cookie and exact ten-code list leave the operation only after known commit; consumed challenges cannot disclose them again. The legacy `system:better-auth` trigger actor is a compatibility label, not proof of the executing runtime, and setup-start telemetry does not assert completed MFA.

nodes.label: Atomic MFA budgets/replay consumption and committed session issuance
nodes.community_name: Rust implementation progress on codex/rust-platform; epic #672 and 55 issues remain the full goal
nodes.norm_label: atomic mfa budgets/replay consumption and committed session issuance
nodes.rationale: Wrong or replayed codes atomically update challenge and account budgets and rejected telemetry. Five failures burn the pending challenge; ten consecutive account failures across challenges lock the account for fifteen minutes, with exact unlock-boundary behavior. A successful code must advance the factor's persisted native TOTP counter, consumes the challenge, resets failure state and creates a fresh twelve-hour session with the existing immutable lifecycle trigger. The session cookie is returned only after known commit. Operational failures roll back all effects; any commit error withholds the cookie and retires the connection for reconciliation. Sensitive bearer wrappers remain non-Debug/non-Serde and owned new buffers zeroize.

Both append distinct accepted events to existing append-only workspace_audit with typed JSON subject/session/audit-version metadata and a user actor; canonical auth telemetry v12 does not permit management endpoint names. No bearer, code or ciphertext enters the audit event. Codes return only after known commit, including audit-only view. Sessions, factor secret/verification, account failures/lock and TOTP replay remain unchanged; pending enrolled-login challenges read only the current replacement pool.

Only response status is inspected; failures are opaque delivery uncertainty, not proof of non-delivery or database rollback.

Four additional native tests plus 106 separate-process/connection checks pass in WAL/DELETE batches: 45 fixed cases per batch, competing database owners, real COMMIT-busy/retained-reader snapshots, revoke/disable/session-delete barriers and killed/reaped children before/after commit. Company sequence and companion effects roll back together on supported precommit failures; known commit survives cleanup failure or postcommit crash, while commit errors/detected transaction escape report unknown. Native callbacks are trusted synchronous code, not SQL sandboxes: COMMIT;BEGIN can evade escape detection and is forbidden. No provider expiry, workspace.json mutation, physical-path lifetime, complete accounting posting, durable idempotency, external-effect recovery or real product writer is qualified by these effect-ledger tests. nodes.label: Generic500ms minimum ACK without constant-time or delivery claim
nodes.community_name: Optional native-only canonical routes and mandatory legacy writer drain
nodes.norm_label: generic500ms minimum ack without constant-time or delivery claim
nodes.rationale: After admission, the existing shared worker permit stays inside blocking work through completion even when the HTTP caller disconnects. Every handler outcome, including unknown commit, delivery error and panic, returns the same 200 {status:true} acknowledgement with a 500 ms minimum after input validation. No bearer, existence, delivery or success assertion is returned. The floor and equal response do not prove constant-time privacy when mail takes longer, and the injected handler must remain bounded. The native application controls real commit/delivery semantics and never automatically reissues a link. The POST rate is three per direct-peer IP per minute, sharing bounded rate/capacity state with identity/recovery; forwarded headers and email/token rotation do not create rate identities. Persistent/distributed/proxy policy remains a separate deployment qualification.

nodes.label: Known invalid unknown completion mappings and sanitized callbacks
nodes.community_name: Optional native-only canonical routes and mandatory legacy writer drain
nodes.norm_label: known invalid unknown completion mappings and sanitized callbacks
nodes.rationale: Only a known native completion returns 200 {status:true,user:null}, or 302 to the prevalidated/sanitized allowed callback. No session/cookie is created. Native invalid/expired/replayed/unissued tokens normalize to 401 INVALID_TOKEN or a fixed error callback. Unknown commit, internal failure and panic yield 503 VERIFICATION_UNCONFIRMED or an error callback; they never yield a success destination. The callback helper inserts no verification bearer and removes reserved token/error/verified query coordinates, preserving other user values/fragments. Responses use no-store/no-referrer/nosniff. General listener/header/TLS/shutdown and host panic-log redaction are not newly qualified here.

nodes.label: Optional native-only canonical routes and mandatory legacy writer drain
nodes.community_name: Optional native-only canonical routes and mandatory legacy writer drain
nodes.norm_label: optional native-only canonical routes and mandatory legacy writer drain
nodes.rationale: AuthHandlers now has optional VerificationHandlers for native persisted request/completion operations on caller-admitted control handles. Its canonical /api/auth/send-verification-email and /api/auth/verify-email paths never dispatch to a legacy handler. With no verification handlers, POST/GET fail closed with 404; HEAD always refuses without consuming a token. The serving owner must route these paths exclusively to Rust and drain the old authoritative verify-email writer before enabling a real deployment. This library/synthetic socket qualification does not close an independently running TypeScript endpoint or qualify physical/lifetime admission, migration or production rollout. The full epic remains open.

nodes.label: Real-socket source-signature/control acceptance and pending gates
nodes.community_name: Optional native-only canonical routes and mandatory legacy writer drain
nodes.norm_label: real-socket source-signature/control acceptance and pending gates
nodes.rationale: Acceptance uses real native sockets plus current synthetic control schemas in WAL/DELETE, actual source cookie/JWT signers, digest/flag/session/audit observations, strict input/query checks, HEAD/replay controls, direct-peer rate checks and actual busy/unknown commits. Native unit tests also inject precommit/unknown/committed/panic outcomes and verify generic timing/body plus fixed callback mapping. UI tests cover recovery without side effects. No external mail, real company data or deployment is used. Scoped GDD is structural readiness only. Remaining service/provider/trusted-device identity, product context, workspace lifetime/legacy writer/restore-lineage qualification, clients/platform/distribution and cutover remain required.

nodes.label: Strict navigation original-token query and no source fallback
nodes.community_name: Optional native-only canonical routes and mandatory legacy writer drain
nodes.norm_label: strict navigation original-token query and no source fallback
nodes.rationale: GET verify-email permits originless cross-site mail navigation but requires exact Host, an actual direct peer and any presented Origin to match. Authorization/service credentials refuse. Query is bounded, accepts only one original compact token and optional callbackURL, rejects percent-encoded token aliases, unknown/duplicate keys, invalid percent/UTF-8 and unsafe callback destinations, and decodes callback exactly once. Callback success processing is validated before native mutation. A fixed operation rate of ten per peer/minute does not use the bearer as a key. HEAD does no dispatch or rate consumption. Tokens signed by the actual source without native context and correctly signed but unissued native envelopes both refuse; there is no source-handler fallback.

nodes.label: Strict send body and optional current session-cookie admission
nodes.community_name: Optional native-only canonical routes and mandatory legacy writer drain
nodes.norm_label: strict send body and optional current session-cookie admission
nodes.rationale: POST send-verification-email requires exact configured Host/Origin, admitted fetch metadata, JSON content, no service/Authorization credential, bounded nonduplicated Cookie header, no query, an 8 KiB body and the existing body deadline. Its strict object accepts only email and optional non-null callbackURL; duplicate/unknown fields, invalid email or unsafe callbacks refuse before native dispatch. Optional session-cookie parsing ignores unrelated cookies but rejects malformed, duplicate or wrong-profile named session credentials, including a bare session-cookie name beside a valid signed value. A signature is only a caller proof; native request processing rechecks the current session/address under its writer. Pending challenge cookies create no session authority.

nodes.community_name: Optional native-only canonical routes and mandatory legacy writer drain
nodes.norm_label: native-only http email verification and fixed recovery ui
nodes.rationale: [Contract](http-verification/CONTRACT.md) adds native-only canonical send/verify routes, strict optional caller/query admission, generic minimum-duration request acknowledgement, known/invalid/unknown completion outcomes and fixed React recovery guidance. Real sockets/source signers and current synthetic controls qualify the bounded surface. Exclusive routing and legacy writer drain remain deployment gates; the full epic remains open.

nodes.label: Atomic original outcome permanent tombstone and checked safe IDs
nodes.community_name: Caller-owned durable keyed receipt storage and source interoperability
nodes.norm_label: atomic original outcome permanent tombstone and checked safe ids
nodes.rationale: Fresh execution invokes synchronous trusted transaction-local Rust code once. Outcome objects may have different property order in serialized JSON; parsed JSON values and source fingerprint bytes are the interoperability contract. Successful domain JSON, append-only tombstone, outcome and idempotency_original audit belong to the same caller transaction. `ok:false`, callback errors, oversized/invalid outcomes and SQL/audit failures are errors requiring whole-transaction rollback, leaving the key reusable. Receipt expires30days after the trusted timestamp. Source-compatible audit event/entity/message/actor fields are retained. No raw key is stored in any receipt or audit. Both generated tombstone and audit IDs use explicit checked positive JavaScript-safe MAX+1; exhausted/poisoned streams refuse rather than SQLite random fallback.

nodes.label: Current authorization before replay and caller transaction rollback obligation
nodes.community_name: Caller-owned durable keyed receipt storage and source interoperability
nodes.norm_label: current authorization before replay and caller transaction rollback obligation
nodes.rationale: The trusted application must authorize the current principal and operation before invoking the primitive, including before replay; input principal and actor are internal facts, never authenticated request claims. The primitive accepts only the seven existing key-idempotent operation names, an explicit user/service-account subject, actor/program, validated business JSON object, mandatory validated client key, and trusted UTC milliseconds. Caller must already admit canonical company schema/physical identity and own a main SQLite write transaction. No connection, transaction, authority or migration is acquired here. Any primitive error requires rollback of the entire caller transaction, including result-shaped `ok:false`; the rejection value is retained for the application. The existing fence releases values only after known commit and retires uncertain handles.

nodes.label: Caller-owned durable keyed receipt storage and source interoperability
nodes.community_name: Caller-owned durable keyed receipt storage and source interoperability
nodes.norm_label: caller-owned durable keyed receipt storage and source interoperability
nodes.rationale: Port `src/core/idempotency.ts` keyed local receipt behavior into a caller-owned main write transaction, suitable for the existing control→company authorization fence. This increment owns storage receipt execution, JSON fingerprints, source interoperability and failure/concurrency checks. Actual manual post/reverse, service company admission, physical lifetime admission, transport endpoints and complete R14 acceptance remain required. Only synthetic disposable data is used.

nodes.label: Explicit outcome pruning and fail-closed stored receipt metadata
nodes.community_name: Caller-owned durable keyed receipt storage and source interoperability
nodes.norm_label: explicit outcome pruning and fail-closed stored receipt metadata
nodes.rationale: Pruning requires the same admitted main writer and deletes only outcomes whose tombstone expires_at<=trusted canonical UTC cutoff. Tombstones and ledger identity remain unchanged and their source triggers remain authoritative. Strict native stored metadata validation rejects malformed ledger UUIDs, receipt IDs, payload hashes, timestamp pairs, duplicate identity matches, oversized/malformed/rejection outcomes and incomplete expiry duration before replay. Malformed metadata is a storage refusal, never a cache miss or new operation.

nodes.label: Lookup-first replay conflict and retained/expired outcome semantics
nodes.community_name: Caller-owned durable keyed receipt storage and source interoperability
nodes.norm_label: lookup-first replay conflict and retained/expired outcome semantics
nodes.rationale: Under the held writer, lookup precedes all domain effects. Same identity and same fingerprint replays the stored JSON outcome and original receipt metadata with a new idempotency_replay audit. Changed fingerprint produces IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT before checking outcome presence. A missing outcome produces IDEMPOTENCY_OUTCOME_EXPIRED, even if its expiry is future. Both refusal audits may be committed only by a caller which has performed no domain effects and deliberately retains the diagnostic; rolling back removes the audit. Clock expiry alone does not suppress a retained outcome: source retention deletes replay material explicitly. Replay never invokes the domain callback.

nodes.label: Source/native concurrent receipt acceptance and revoked-replay fence
nodes.community_name: Caller-owned durable keyed receipt storage and source interoperability
nodes.norm_label: source/native concurrent receipt acceptance and revoked-replay fence
nodes.rationale: Acceptance compares actual installed source executor and native executor on canonical synthetic company DBs: key/Unicode/numeric canonicalization, new/replay/conflict/pruned and retained expiry behavior, principal/operation/ledger isolation, key rotation/actor/path independence, business rejection and late SQL rollback, immutable tombstones, bounded IDs, actual concurrent same-key writers and process death before commit. Compose with the real current human authorization fence to prove revoked replay does not invoke receipt lookup or disclose outcomes. Source-generated receipts must replay natively and native receipts must replay through the source implementation. These checks qualify storage composition, not a deployed posting endpoint or full engine completion.

nodes.label: Stable ledger/principal/key receipt identity and exact UTF16/JSON fingerprint
nodes.community_name: Caller-owned durable keyed receipt storage and source interoperability
nodes.norm_label: stable ledger/principal/key receipt identity and exact utf16/json fingerprint
nodes.rationale: Receipt identity is SHA256 of the original UTF8 key, current immutable ledger UUID, operation, principal kind and exact stable subject. Key validation follows JavaScript UTF16 length1..128 and ECMAScript trim nonemptiness without trimming the stored key. Actor, program, credential, path and workspace/company display selectors are excluded. Actor/program use ECMAScript trimming before source audit rendering; explicit actor/program input bounds are512/256 UTF8 bytes and empty components refuse. Payload fingerprint recursively sorts object keys by UTF16 code units, preserves array order, uses JSON.stringify-compatible strings and correctly rounded binary64 parsing (`serde_json/float_roundtrip`) and number rendering, and hashes at most65536 UTF8 bytes. Business payload must already exclude transport confirm/idempotencyKey. Native typed boundary rejects unsafe integer-valued JSON numbers, nesting beyond64, lone surrogates and non-object business roots; these explicit stricter refusals do not reinterpret source receipts.

nodes.label: Durable keyed mutation receipts storage increment
nodes.community_name: Caller-owned durable keyed receipt storage and source interoperability
nodes.norm_label: durable keyed mutation receipts storage increment
nodes.rationale: `idempotency-1` adds caller-transaction receipt execution and source/native replay interoperability, canonical UTF16/JSON fingerprints, permanent key tombstones, explicit retention and same-transaction audits. Current human authorization is checked before lookup/replay through the existing fence. [Contract](idempotency/CONTRACT.md), [readiness](idempotency/readiness.json) and [evidence](idempotency/evidence.json). Actual manual posting/reversal, domain gates and service company admission remain the next R14/R13 work; this storage increment does not close those issues or enable deployed writes.

nodes.label: Success, usage and ledger-rejection exit codes
nodes.description: 0 means ok true, 2 means parsing/usage, 1 means valid call rejected by ledger; JSON business output is stdout while parse errors go to stderr.
nodes.norm_label: success, usage and ledger-rejection exit codes

nodes.label: Opt-in overdue weekly-backup lock
nodes.description: BEK205 backup overdue after grace window refuses bookkeeping writes with conflict until backup.

nodes.label: Exact valued --confirm yes CLI gate
nodes.description: Confirm is valued exact yes for destructive and documented external operations; ordinary writes rely on actor; MCP requires true for all writes.

nodes.label: Exact-event-hash independent draft review
nodes.description: Draft create/revise/submit/reject/approve binds current eventHash; session supplies actor; independent reviewer posts atomically after revalidation; exact retries return evidence.

nodes.label: Stable HTTP error envelope and subcodes
nodes.description: Errors use ok false, errors[], HTTP code and optional finer subcode; CSRF/content-type and confirm markers avoid message parsing.
nodes.norm_label: stable http error envelope and subcodes

nodes.label: Explicit actor allowlist in policy.yaml
nodes.description: Explicit canonical actors must be allowlisted; derived environment actors are documented as not allowlist-checked.

nodes.label: Principal-derived per-request ActorContext
nodes.description: Explicit core ActorContext comes from auth rather than process env, preventing parallel request identity collisions.

nodes.label: Explicit-date profile-bound group reporting
nodes.description: Group reads require explicit asOf; approved profile plus from/asOf bounds consolidation; hosted filtering happens before aggregation.

nodes.label: Hosted Better Auth session and company permissions
nodes.description: Hosted identity is checked against append-only membership and declared route permission before company ledger opens; local/bearer seams also documented.
nodes.norm_label: hosted better auth session and company permissions

nodes.label: Cockpit irreversible-write confirmation
nodes.description: Irreversible entry writes require confirm true; invoice issue and exception resolve rely on modal consent; MCP/CLI conventions differ.

nodes.label: withCompanyMutation shared write pipeline
nodes.description: Localhost gate, company resolution, confirm, open/migrate, backup lock, actor and core business-result mapping define writes.

nodes.label: Restore actor policy uses target-company
nodes.description: Mutation policy is checked at restore destination where writes occur, rather than source company.

nodes.label: Canonical and environment-derived CLI actors
nodes.description: Mutations resolve explicit --actor, RENTEMESTER_ACTOR then prioritized environment actor; read-only calls need no actor.

nodes.label: Read-only migration plan and atomic apply
nodes.description: No apply gives read-only wouldMigrate; actor-authorized IMMEDIATE transaction rechecks state and emits one schema_migrated event if pending migration commits.
nodes.norm_label: read-only migration plan and atomic apply

nodes.label: Built cockpit static SPA fallback
nodes.description: Non-api routes serve app/dist index fallback; missing build yields root health and otherwise JSON404.

nodes.label: Queued DigiSense status-only observation
nodes.description: Previously queued identity can only call document-status and append evidence; never invokes delivery.

nodes.label: Workspace HTTP API over the shared bookkeeping core
nodes.description: React cockpit or HTTP client calls same src/core as MCP and agent run; company routes resolve workspace slugs.
nodes.norm_label: workspace http api over the shared bookkeeping core

nodes.label: Allowlisted SQL-view drift repair
nodes.description: Read-only plan; explicit apply requires actor and reason, repairs only built-in catalog under IMMEDIATE transaction and one atomic audit event.

nodes.label: Command-specific CLI read shapes
nodes.description: Reads have no shared envelope/parity; array/rows and snake_case differ from MCP camelCase; each command shape is inspected directly.

nodes.label: Company-bound DigiSense invoice delivery
nodes.description: Server resolves local company transport identity and credentials; acknowledged retries do not redeliver.

nodes.label: Flat CLI write output and MCP field parity
nodes.description: Writes return same result fields as MCP data but at CLI top level with ok/errors/appliedRules, never data-wrapped.
nodes.norm_label: flat cli write output and mcp field parity

nodes.label: Country and identifier-kind supplier resolution
nodes.description: non_eu may omit VAT/CVR; EU reverse charge requires VAT number and existing VIES evidence; conflicts demand human_resolution_required.

nodes.label: Agent determinism
nodes.rationale: Automatiseret bogføring skal reproducere beslutningsgrundlag og respektere eksplicitte stop-/reviewgrænser.

nodes.label: Agentens mutationsgrænser
nodes.rationale: Agenten stopper ved reviewkrævende eller ikke-deterministiske forhold.

nodes.label: Periodisk agent-loop
nodes.rationale: Runtime-agenten følger en begrænset read/decide/act/report cyklus.

nodes.label: Runtime bogholder-agent
nodes.rationale: Agenten kører en begrænset periodisk bogføringssløjfe med determinisme og hårde sikkerhedsgrænser.

nodes.label: Atomic verified flag/lifecycle/audit without access or session grant
nodes.community_name: Admitted persisted email issuance/completion without HTTP or mail
nodes.norm_label: atomic verified flag/lifecycle/audit without access or session grant
nodes.rationale: Success deletes exactly that issuance, sets only the subject's emailVerified=1 and updatedAt, and appends completion audit plus accepted verify-email telemetry in the same transaction. The existing trigger appends the email_verified lifecycle event. No account, factor, workspace access or session is created or changed. Other outstanding sibling rows may remain, but the verified flag and lifecycle change render them unusable. Existing sessions are preserved, matching the configured source behavior; no automatic sign-in is granted. All failures before commit roll back, and connection reuse requires successful rollback plus preflight. An uncertain commit returns OutcomeUnknown, retires the handle and releases no bearer or success result. SQL/claims/bearers never appear in public errors.

nodes.label: Digest-only intent with exact current user/nullable credentials/lifecycle binding
nodes.community_name: Admitted persisted email issuance/completion without HTTP or mail
nodes.norm_label: digest-only intent with exact current user/nullable credentials/lifecycle binding
nodes.rationale: `issue` folds the address using the shared practical ASCII email policy. Connection preflight precedes input acceptance and reuse claims. Under an immediate control writer, it samples time once, signs a native token and persists only a SHA-256 bearer digest identifier in the existing verification table. The value binds the exact current subject/address/workspace, user creation/update and MFA flag, ordered credential rows with explicit NULL markers, and immutable credential/email/MFA/session-revocation lifecycle count. Credential rows are bounded and their sensitive strings zeroized where supported. Address verification is independent of workspace membership: it grants no role or access. Unknown and already-verified addresses create no intent and return internal None. Internal Some(token) is released only after a known successful commit. A public adapter must conceal account existence and must not expose this result directly.

nodes.rationale: Before enabling native send-verification-email/verify-email, implement the mail/redirect and HTTP policies, public generic acknowledgement, rate limits and caller/session checks. Close the legacy authoritative /verify-email bypass at the same enablement boundary: it accepts native JWTs but ignores persisted context. Native persistence cannot make that parallel legacy handler safe. Physical/lifetime writer admission, recovery-lineage qualification, service/provider parity, clients/distribution and all remaining epic acceptance remain required. Real mail and production changes retain their existing mandates.

nodes.label: Fresh writer-time original-bearer verification and unchanged-context completion
nodes.community_name: Admitted persisted email issuance/completion without HTTP or mail
nodes.norm_label: fresh writer-time original-bearer verification and unchanged-context completion
nodes.rationale: `complete` receives the original bearer, never a previously verified proof. It begins an immediate transaction and samples trusted time only after writer admission. Signature, native purpose/workspace/active key and exact one-hour validity are reverified using that single sample. The digest must select exactly one persisted intent with exact issuance/expiry timestamps and unchanged context. Current email lookup must still resolve the originally bound subject, with emailVerified=0 and unchanged credential/lifecycle facts. Recycled addresses, changed/replaced credentials, changed user/MFA context, duplicate/corrupt intent, expiry and replay refuse. Updating and restoring a password still advances immutable lifecycle evidence and invalidates the link.

nodes.label: Admitted persisted email issuance/completion without HTTP or mail
nodes.community_name: Admitted persisted email issuance/completion without HTTP or mail
nodes.norm_label: admitted persisted email issuance/completion without http or mail
nodes.rationale: This increment connects the native purpose-bound email token to one-time persisted issuance and an atomic application operation. The caller supplies an already admitted control connection, trusted workspace/current signing key, trusted Clock and audit key version. It does not enable an HTTP endpoint, send mail, migrate real data or qualify legacy dual writers. The full Rust epic remains open.

nodes.label: WAL/DELETE current-fact/process acceptance and structural scope
nodes.community_name: Admitted persisted email issuance/completion without HTTP or mail
nodes.norm_label: wal/delete current-fact/process acceptance and structural scope
nodes.rationale: The process acceptance suite uses actual current synthetic control schemas and separate Rust processes in WAL and DELETE modes. It checks digest-only persistence, exact effects and protected-state preservation, replay/sibling refusal, exact restoration and NULL-to-empty replacement, address recycling, duplicate/corrupt rows, current facts after writer admission, single-writer serialization, SQL rollback, known/unknown commit and malformed input on unready handles. The GDD report proves structural readiness for this bounded application operation, not full feature parity or deployment authority.

Mail/HTTP/public policy and legacy verification-bypass closure remain required before enablement; this increment does not complete the epic.

nodes.label: Immutable auth lifecycle count exemption and no repair inference
nodes.norm_label: immutable auth lifecycle count exemption and no repair inference
nodes.rationale: The auth lifecycle evidence table is different: native pending MFA uses a count of immutable relevant events, so its full-width IDs must remain accepted. Do not conflate arbitrary audit/evidence tables or unrelated company sequence domains with these three ordered streams. No automatic renumbering, timestamp fallback, deletion, permissive first-row selection or inferred repair is allowed. Unsupported history requires an explicit reviewed migration/recovery decision before runtime exposure.

nodes.label: Independent stream boundary and legacy comparison acceptance
nodes.norm_label: independent stream boundary and legacy comparison acceptance
nodes.rationale: Acceptance: real TypeScript canonical migrations and independent native processes in WAL/DELETE; each ordered stream at maximum and after automatic lower-ID allocation refuses with exact control/company image preservation, while largest-minus-one still permits current control observations. Demonstrate actual legacy stale-grant behavior on private synthetic copies and native refusal. Retain existing full-width auth-lifecycle MFA test and all affected identity/fence checks. No real company data or production writes.

nodes.label: Maximum ROWID random allocation hazard and max-minus-one boundary
nodes.norm_label: maximum rowid random allocation hazard and max-minus-one boundary
nodes.rationale: Those streams select current state by numeric ID. At the largest ROWID SQLite may allocate subsequent automatic IDs randomly below the largest, so a later disable/revoke can be hidden by an earlier grant. Refuse the exhausted stream even before a later lower row exists. Its immutable maximum row keeps the refusal sticky. Largest-minus-one remains readable: numeric ordering still holds until the next insertion; existing writer fences and locked current-state rechecks continue to govern races. This does not authorize new access-event writers or prove arbitrary explicit historical IDs were chronological.

nodes.label: Opaque no-effect refusal and explicit legacy incompatibility
nodes.norm_label: opaque no-effect refusal and explicit legacy incompatibility
nodes.rationale: Refusal is the existing opaque invalid_control failure at credential/session/current-access boundaries. Roll back without company effects, challenges, sessions, counters or audit writes and preserve caller source images. Never interpret unsupported history as authenticated identity or grant. This gate does not repair legacy TypeScript authorization, whose actual stale-grant observation must remain an explicit incompatibility; full legacy writer enrollment, physical handle/lifetime admission, endpoint and cutover qualification remain pending.

nodes.label: Global ordered authorization-event exhaustion admission
nodes.rationale: Admit an existing canonical control handle only while none of the three append-only numeric-order streams contains SQLite's largest signed ROWID, 9223372036854775807: rm_workspace_user_access_events, rm_company_membership_events and rm_workspace_security_events. Check all three globally, including rows for other subjects or companies, inside the caller's already held control transaction and after exact schema/history/integrity admission. This is a native runtime admission correction; do not change rows, migrations or source files on disk.

nodes.rationale: When a customer invoice loss is established, Rentemester must write off only the remaining principal receivable through an append-only invoice-linked correction entry so the audit trail remains deterministic; non-DKK write-offs must reuse the invoice’s fixed FX basis for the DKK ledger relief.

nodes.label: Full invoice must contain core seller/buyer/date/number/content fields
nodes.norm_label: full invoice must contain core seller/buyer/date/number/content fields

nodes.label: Issued invoices must be stored immutably with sequential invoice numbers
nodes.norm_label: issued invoices must be stored immutably with sequential invoice numbers
nodes.rationale: Rentemester must only issue invoices after deterministic validation and must persist an immutable issued snapshot tied to a sequential invoice number; when the invoice currency is not DKK, the snapshot must include the chosen FX rate and DKK totals fixed at issue time.

nodes.label: Issued invoices cannot be modified
nodes.rationale: Corrections to issued invoices are handled via credit note and new invoice, not mutation.

nodes.label: Invoice payments must be traceably applied against issued invoices and bank transactions
nodes.norm_label: invoice payments must be traceably applied against issued invoices and bank transactions
nodes.rationale: Rentemester must track which issued invoice a payment settles, how much was applied, and whether any balance remains open.

nodes.label: Invoice preview must render the issued-invoice PDF without mutating the ledger
nodes.norm_label: invoice preview must render the issued-invoice pdf without mutating the ledger
nodes.rationale: Rentemester's "Forhåndsvis"-flow (#440) must run the same validator + renderer as the irreversible issue path so the owner sees the exact PDF the customer will receive, but without drawing a fortløbende invoice number, without writing a documents row, and without appending to audit_log — a closed preview must leave the ledger and sequence-serie untouched.

nodes.label: Simplified invoice is only allowed up to DKK 3,000 gross and needs the reduced field set
nodes.norm_label: simplified invoice is only allowed up to dkk 3,000 gross and needs the reduced field set
nodes.rationale: Rentemester must reject simplified invoices above DKK 3,000 gross or without the mandatory reduced content set.

nodes.label: Recurring invoice generation is explicit, deterministic and idempotent per template period
nodes.norm_label: recurring invoice generation is explicit, deterministic and idempotent per template period
nodes.rationale: Rentemester materialises a recurring invoice only on an explicit generate call for a given as-of date; the issue date and delivery period are derived deterministically from the template's first issue date and interval, and a unique template/period audit link prevents duplicate generation across reruns.

nodes.label: Recurring invoice templates store an immutable, pre-validated invoice specification
nodes.norm_label: recurring invoice templates store an immutable, pre-validated invoice specification
nodes.rationale: A recurring invoice template captures the repeating invoice (interval, customer, lines, VAT, delivery-period mode) as an append-only, pre-validated specification so every generated invoice is reproducible; the embedded payload must already satisfy the full-invoice rules before the template can be created.

Full management UI, company/dispatch fencing and platform delivery open.

nodes.label: Native service admission and workspace-context increment
nodes.norm_label: native service admission and workspace-context increment
nodes.rationale: Source-issued native GET /api/me uses current registry/access, bounded own context and atomic persisted quota/refill/inactivity-rate admission. Human/service credentials exclusive; counters commit before disclosure. Expiry/typing/atomicity/source-CAS boundary corrections explicit. Full lifecycle/company-dispatch fencing/adapters/runtime/cutover remain pending.

nodes.label: Atomic source-compatible principal and random credential issuance
nodes.norm_label: atomic source-compatible principal and random credential issuance
nodes.rationale: Create/rotate/revoke commit pending/completed operation events, exact key/registry/user effects and service events together. New service_UUIDhex/@service.invalid flags0 creates no account/password/session/access/membership. OS-random UUID4 and rms_ plus64 uniform ASCII letters hash SHA256 UTF8/base64url; source marker/name/start/prefix and default600/60000 unlimited quota/refill. Default90days; optional expiry1..365days seconds. No caller secret/hash/id/actor authority.

nodes.label: Bounded nonsecret credential inventory for deliberate lost-secret cleanup
nodes.norm_label: bounded nonsecret credential inventory for deliberate lost-secret cleanup
nodes.rationale: Preserve source registry created_at/user_id ordering and enabled count including expired/NULL rows, not live-auth count. Add owner-only credentialId/nullable-enabled/expiresAt entries; no raw key/hash/marker/metadata/email. Maximum1000 principals/1000 credentials/1MiB; malformed names/flags/dates/overflow refuse whole list. Strict source UTC or ISO dates; retain stored createdAt. Inventory/readback enables explicit inaccessible-key cleanup.

nodes.label: Known-commit-only one-time secret receipt and uncertain handle retirement
nodes.norm_label: known-commit-only one-time secret receipt and uncertain handle retirement
nodes.rationale: Bounded create201/rotate200 receipt includes ok/operationId/serviceAccountId/credentialId/secret; revoke ok/operationId/revoked. Late schema/SQL/serialization failure or precommit death rolls back rows/events/flags. Every commit error retires handle, returns OutcomeUnknown without receipt/secret or unchanged-state/replay claim. Zeroizing non-Debug/Clone/Serialize wrappers do not promise secure SQLite/process/HTTP/browser erasure.

nodes.label: Lost-reply recovery readback and atomic cleanup after actual worker drain
nodes.norm_label: lost-reply recovery readback and atomic cleanup after actual worker drain
nodes.rationale: Completed returns completed/recovered:false; recovered returns recovered:true, with nonsecret account/credential/replacement IDs, never secret. Lost secret can be explicitly revoked with new operation ID. Recovering age<30000ms unchanged; equality expired. Pending/failed/expired recovery under held writer disables only own/config/marker replacements then failed/recovered for create/rotate, never reactivating old. Revoke disables bound present target then event/completed; absent target completes without fabricated event, foreign/config mismatch refuses. No persisted claim needed only conditional on actual legacy drain; source transient states remain truthful on refusal/unknown.

nodes.label: Native owner service credential lifecycle
nodes.rationale: Owner-only native list/create/rotate/revoke/recover and five existing workspace service-principal HTTP paths use admitted control connections. Atomic native recovery still requires actual legacy/provider worker drain; expired recovering lease or SQLite lock cannot fence a later external provider-create. No real runtime admission, deployment or full platform completion.

nodes.label: Optional strict lifecycle HTTP routes and shared direct-peer admission
nodes.norm_label: optional strict lifecycle http routes and shared direct-peer admission
nodes.rationale: Optional handler owns paths with404/no fallback. GET rejects query/body/encoding; HEAD405 no dispatch/rate. Mutation exact JSON fields and confirm:true, optional nonnull UUID and integer expiry create/rotate; arrays/duplicates/unknown subject/actor/secret refuse. Current signed human cookie, Host/Origin/fetch, no service/Authorization,8192byte/2second/four-worker gates; optional list Origin, exact mutation Origin. Shared10/min peer bucket ignores forwarded/targets/IDs. Known success bounded no-cookie no-store/no-referrer/nosniff; invalid401/input400/reused409/operational-malformed-unknown-panic503 with no partial receipt. No retry/logged plaintext; issuance HTTP necessarily contains secret.

nodes.label: Owner human session authority and fresh mutation consent
nodes.norm_label: owner human session authority and fresh mutation consent
nodes.rationale: Canonical BEGIN IMMEDIATE resolves runtime cookie, verified email, enabled strict verified MFA and active workspace_owner, never service/member/request actor. List uses Current12h and rollback without refresh/audit; mutations/recovery Fresh<10minutes. Explicit confirm:true is consent, not authentication. Bound actor/user/inputs.

nodes.label: Precise bound-key rotation and revocation without reactivation
nodes.norm_label: precise bound-key rotation and revocation without reactivation
nodes.rationale: Rotation preserves subject, disables exact owner/config target and creates one replacement even if target already disabled. Revoke disables exact bound key including NULL-enabled with event. Missing/wrong-owner/config direct targets refuse with no writes; old keys never reactivated or deleted.

nodes.label: Strict recovery stream transitions, marker binding and checked event IDs
nodes.norm_label: strict recovery stream transitions, marker binding and checked event ids
nodes.rationale: Validate complete numeric-ID-ordered stream: initial pending; stable type/subject/marker/old key; allowed pending→completed/failed/recovering, failed→recovering/recovered, recovering→recovering/completed/failed; terminal never reopen. Strict bounded UUID/actor/marker/nonfuture UTC/ISO dates/status fields, registered subject and max1000 rows. Cross-operation marker reuse refuses. Both service event streams require positive IDs/no MAX poison; explicit checked MAX+1 prevents random ROWID fallback and rolls back MAX−1 multiappend overflow.

nodes.label: Synthetic source interoperability, recovery crash states and remaining delivery gates
nodes.norm_label: synthetic source interoperability, recovery crash states and remaining delivery gates
nodes.rationale: WAL/DELETE/source owner cookies/provider verification and rotation cover precise effects/no implicit access, one-time secrets/reuse/lost cleanup, inventory, authority/input refusals, concurrency/writer exclusion/late rollback/death/DELETE unknown. Rehearse source pre/post-provider and old-disable crash/failed-compensation histories; strict30s, transitions/markers/MAX headroom. No full management UI, service company/dispatch fence, actual legacy drain, CLI/MCP/GPUI/distribution/cutover or complete epic issue qualification.

nodes.label: Caller-known normalized operation IDs and no automatic replay
nodes.norm_label: caller-known normalized operation ids and no automatic replay
nodes.rationale: Trim UUIDv1..8 variant89ab to lowercase; optional new mutation ID generates UUID4. Recovery needs known operationId. Future clients should preassign IDs because a lost autogenerated ID cannot be guessed/retried. Any used operationId, completed/failed/recovered included, refuses reuse and cannot redisclose secret.

nodes.label: Scoped Graphify navigation
nodes.rationale: Use query, path and explain before raw inspection, then verify findings in source. Use the wiki for broad navigation and reserve the full report for architecture review or insufficient scoped context.

nodes.rationale: Code changes require graphify update . before committing and finishing. Readonly subagents leave writes to the main agent; worktrees require explicit updates because Git hooks skip them.

nodes.label: Mandatory Graphify-first codebase workflow
nodes.rationale: Main agents and subagents query from the active checkout before questions, analysis, development, debugging, reviews or refactoring. No slash command is needed; dirty output is not an exception. Only explicit user opt-out or graph repair permits skipping.

nodes.label: Semantic refresh with preserved content and honest pending sources
nodes.norm_label: semantic refresh with preserved content and honest pending sources
nodes.rationale: Changed documents, rules and images require semantic updates. Preserve old semantic content, disclose pending sources, and never report AST updates as semantic extraction.

nodes.label: Graph build provenance, diagnostics and unavailable native token usage
nodes.norm_label: graph build provenance, diagnostics and unavailable native token usage
nodes.rationale: Build metadata records source fingerprints, versions, extraction limits and pending sources. Graph diagnostics are separate; unavailable token usage is disclosed instead of reported as zero.

nodes.label: Claude Code search and first-read Graphify guards
nodes.norm_label: claude code search and first-read graphify guards
nodes.rationale: Bash|Grep use hook-guard search; Read|Glob use hook-guard read --strict. The first applicable raw read is denied once per session, not permanently; agent instructions remain authoritative.

nodes.label: Codex Graphify integration through AGENTS.md and the skill
nodes.norm_label: codex graphify integration through agents.md and the skill
nodes.rationale: Codex uses AGENTS.md and the skill; installed hook-check is a no-op, so the obsolete hook entry is removed instead of claimed as enforcement.

nodes.label: Background Git-hook AST refresh with linked-worktree exclusion
nodes.norm_label: background git-hook ast refresh with linked-worktree exclusion
nodes.rationale: Post-commit and post-checkout refresh the primary checkout in the background and skip linked worktrees. Status proves installation only; inspect logs for completion. Hooks neither perform semantic extraction nor enforce query-first behavior.

nodes.label: Local Graphify installation, SQL support and Git merge-driver configuration
nodes.norm_label: local graphify installation, sql support and git merge-driver configuration
nodes.rationale: CLI upgrades include SQL parsing. Hook installation preserves existing hooks and registers the merge driver; committed attributes do not install local executables or driver configuration on another clone.

nodes.label: Binding agent instructions for Graphify queries and explicit updates
nodes.norm_label: binding agent instructions for graphify queries and explicit updates
nodes.rationale: AGENTS.md binds main agents and subagents to query first, verify source and update explicitly before code commits and completion, including in linked worktrees.

nodes.label: Full semantic rebuild through native agents or headless backend
nodes.norm_label: full semantic rebuild through native agents or headless backend
nodes.rationale: Native session agents require no separate API key; headless extraction needs a configured backend. Incremental updates preserve existing semantics; force means intentional full replacement.

nodes.label: Emailing an invoice or reminder must be deterministic, idempotent, and recorded in an append-only send log
nodes.norm_label: emailing an invoice or reminder must be deterministic, idempotent, and recorded in an append-only send log
nodes.rationale: Rentemester may email an issued invoice or a payment reminder to the customer with the rendered PDF attached, but only deterministically and idempotently. The MIME message and its message-id must be fully derived from the content so an identical send collapses onto the existing append-only send-log row instead of silently re-transmitting. A send is recorded in the send log (recipient, document, message-id, timestamp) and audit-linked; a transport failure writes no success row. SMTP credentials and SMTP configuration stay outside core bookkeeping state — they are sourced from a config file or environment, never persisted to the ledger. The send must fail clearly on a missing customer email or missing SMTP config.

nodes.label: Canonical envelope authenticated UTF8/BOM and owned-buffer zeroization
nodes.community_name: Native existing MFA cryptographic primitives without lifecycle authority
nodes.norm_label: canonical envelope authenticated utf8/bom and owned-buffer zeroization
nodes.rationale: Envelope versions are canonical decimal with no signs, whitespace, suffixes, exponent or leading zero except0. This deliberately rejects source parseInt permissiveness. Lowercase even hex, minimum40 decoded bytes and maximum4096 plaintext UTF8 bytes are enforced before unbounded allocation. Empty plaintext is supported by the encryption primitive. Authenticated non-UTF8 plaintext refuses rather than using JavaScript replacement decoding. As with the source TextDecoder, decryption strips exactly one leading UTF8 BOM and preserves subsequent/interior BOMs; encryption preserves the input bytes, so BOM-prefixed plaintext is not a byte-identical encrypt/decrypt round trip. Keyring keys, plaintext and encrypted-value wrappers have no Debug/Clone/Serde; explicit accessors are for trusted persistence/verification only. Owned derived keys and plaintext working/output buffers zeroize on drop, with in-place AEAD and capacity reserved before plaintext copy. Input, dependency internals, compiler/allocator/register/OS copies are outside erasure claims.

nodes.label: Empty associated data identity and key-rotation boundary
nodes.community_name: Native existing MFA cryptographic primitives without lifecycle authority
nodes.norm_label: empty associated data identity and key-rotation boundary

nodes.label: Explicit keyring and salt-string-derived XChaCha envelope
nodes.community_name: Native existing MFA cryptographic primitives without lifecycle authority
nodes.norm_label: explicit keyring and salt-string-derived xchacha envelope
nodes.rationale: A trusted caller explicitly injects an ordered keyring of1–16 unique nonnegative JavaScript-safe integer versions, first active, plus optional explicit legacy secret. Each key string is canonical unpadded base64url encoding of at least32 bytes, bounded to4096 ASCII bytes. Original entropy is not recoverable or proved by encoding. Encryption derives a32-byte key as SHA256 of the secret STRING's UTF8 bytes, not decoded entropy. XChaCha20-Poly1305 uses a fresh OS-random24-byte nonce, empty additional data, and stores lowercase hex of nonce||ciphertext||16-byte tag. New values always use $ba$VERSION$HEX with the first configured version. Decode selects exactly that declared version; historical keys decrypt only. Bare hex requires the explicit legacy key and never falls back to current/other keys. Missing/retired versions and malformed/authentication failures return opaque invalid_credentials; invalid configuration is invalid_auth_config and OS entropy failure is auth_crypto_unavailable. No environment key fallback exists.

Compare native OTP with independently calculated counters and actual installed createOTP using a controlled test clock, including boundaries, future/past windows, wrong code, grammar, secret and clock limits. Preserve secret-free process evidence and native existing password/cookie/login checks. Review and fix concrete findings before delivery. Stop at verified runtime crypto; actual pending challenge/MFA/session/recovery/endpoint, physical SQLite-handle/lifetime admission, cross-platform storage and complete R04/R41/cutover stay pending.
