nodes.label: OS-entropy uniform enrollment secret generation
nodes.community_name: Native existing MFA cryptographic primitives without lifecycle authority
nodes.rationale: Enrollment secret generation produces32 characters uniformly from the existing64-character ASCII alphabet using OS entropy, yielding192 random bits. No fixed seed, environment source or caller nonce/counter is available in production issuance. Deterministic nonces/counters are test-only helpers. Native TOTP verifier takes a trusted Clock, never a caller/request time claim. No SHA1 signing/security protocol is introduced beyond the existing RFC4226/6238 HMAC OTP profile.

nodes.label: Primary crypto references and constant-time platform limits
nodes.community_name: Native existing MFA cryptographic primitives without lifecycle authority
nodes.norm_label: primary crypto references and constant-time platform limits
nodes.rationale: Primary references: https://docs.rs/chacha20poly1305/0.10.1/chacha20poly1305/ ; https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc4226 ; https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6238 . RustCrypto's constant-time claim depends on constant-time integer multiplication on the target; this increment verifies the current macOS ARM64 host, not every platform or hardware fault mode.

nodes.label: Trusted-clock direct-secret TOTP window and highest counter
nodes.community_name: Native existing MFA cryptographic primitives without lifecycle authority
nodes.norm_label: trusted-clock direct-secret totp window and highest counter
nodes.rationale: TOTP is HMAC-SHA1 over the eight-byte unsigned big-endian counter floor(unix_milliseconds/30000), using the secret STRING's UTF8 bytes directly; do not base32-decode it. Provisioning's base32 wraps those original bytes. Dynamic truncation modulo1000000 produces exactly six ASCII digits. Verify all three counters[-1,0,+1] around a trusted runtime Clock without early successful return, with constant-time fixed-length code comparisons; return the highest matching counter for future durable replay enforcement. Code must be exactly six ASCII digits; secret1–1024 UTF8 bytes; clock0 through9999-12-31T23:59:59.999Z. Negative/unavailable clock refuses invalid_auth_clock. A negative neighboring counter at the epoch is skipped rather than wrapping to2^64-1 as JavaScript DataView permits. Other malformed inputs return invalid_credentials. This match is not one-time consumption, challenge expiry/attempt budgets/account lockout, current enrollment or session authorization: those require a held control transaction and persistent lifecycle state.

nodes.label: Current canonical BigInt roundtrip and transport budget refinement
nodes.community_name: Shared pure exact decimal value contract
nodes.norm_label: current canonical bigint roundtrip and transport budget refinement
nodes.rationale: Canonical serde validates fixed-scale strings directly: money two decimals, rate six, currency three letters. Reject numeric JSON/exponents/plus/leading zeros/negative zero/wrong scale/whitespace/noncanonical output; typed errors expose no partial values. Do not reapply raw2048-byte/exponent limits to canonical decoding: arithmetic may yield larger exact valid BigInts and every serialized typed value must roundtrip. No separate canonical digit domain maximum; future transports must enforce request byte budgets before decoding, without qualifying an unbounded endpoint.

nodes.label: Currency grammar and FX caller authority
nodes.community_name: Shared pure exact decimal value contract
nodes.norm_label: currency grammar and fx caller authority
nodes.rationale: Currency is exactly three uppercase ASCII letters including synthetic/configured codes, with no trim/default/Unicode normalization or registry certification. Adapters own normalization and configured eligibility; callers retain currency/quote identity. Applying FxRate proves neither conversion authority nor journal evidence.

nodes.label: Exact arithmetic independent acceptance and scope boundary
nodes.community_name: Shared pure exact decimal value contract
nodes.norm_label: exact arithmetic independent acceptance and scope boundary
nodes.rationale: Require native signed/half/raw-versus-prequantized/rate/bounds/division/canonical cases, independent Python Decimal expectations and actual TypeScript observations. Separate source precision/binary FX differences and native admission without erasing discrepancies. Preserve Money/read/report/hash behavior and prior suites; verify pure dependency/I-O boundaries, scoped GDD readiness and independent review. No persisted-format/TypeScript/production-data/writer-authority/full FX policy/legal/UI/broad R09 or epic completion.

nodes.label: Operation-specific exact quantization stages
nodes.community_name: Shared pure exact decimal value contract
nodes.rationale: Money.multiply_decimal parses two raw operands and rounds their product once to cents. Money.percent uses a cent amount and percent rounded to two-decimal basis points. FxRate.parse rounds to six decimals and refuses nonpositive rounded rates; apply multiplies prequantized cents by rate and rounds once. Shared signed rounded division handles all signs/halves/zero denominator.

nodes.label: Shared pure exact decimal value contract
nodes.community_name: Shared pure exact decimal value contract
nodes.norm_label: shared pure exact decimal value contract
nodes.rationale: Continue bounded R09 with private shared arbitrary-precision decimal grammar, no float/new dependency or wrapping. Raw input remains ASCII decimal/exponent <=2048 bytes, exponent -400..400 and half-away quantization; resource limits are not configured business maxima.

nodes.label: Atomic challenge failures and cross-challenge account lock budget
nodes.community_name: Internal enrolled TOTP login transaction and pending deployment gates
nodes.norm_label: atomic challenge failures and cross-challenge account lock budget
nodes.rationale: Each wrong/malformed/replayed TOTP code commits one challenge failure and one account failure, plus rejected telemetry, under the same lock. Burn all three pending records immediately on the fifth failure (a deliberate correction to source cleanup on the next attempt). Account budget spans fresh password challenges; tenth consecutive failure locks 15 minutes. No issuance or verification bypasses a future lockedUntil. At/after exact lock expiry, failure counting starts from 0. Missing/NULL account counter means 0; negative/oversized/malformed state refuses. Operational decryption/clock/SQL/admission failures roll back, do not spend attempts, and never become authentication success.

nodes.label: Internal enrolled TOTP login transaction and pending deployment gates
nodes.community_name: Internal enrolled TOTP login transaction and pending deployment gates
nodes.norm_label: internal enrolled totp login transaction and pending deployment gates
nodes.rationale: Outcome: compose the native password and MFA crypto into enrolled-user challenge issuance and atomic TOTP verification/session creation on an already admitted caller-owned canonical control connection. No HTTP listener or real workspace path is opened. Actual SQLite-handle/workspace lifetime admission, endpoint origin/rate/bounded blocking and production cutover remain mandatory before exposure. Unenrolled users get EnrollmentRequired after valid password, without a session or setup authority; actual enrollment, backup recovery, trusted devices and rememberMe variants remain pending.

nodes.label: Locked current challenge/context and trusted-clock admission
nodes.community_name: Internal enrolled TOTP login transaction and pending deployment gates
nodes.norm_label: locked current challenge/context and trusted-clock admission
nodes.rationale: Verify the signed challenge and current records under one control BEGIN IMMEDIATE. Require exactly one challenge/attempt/context record, canonical ISO UTC millisecond dates, created<=now<expires, positive TTL<=600000, equal creation/expiry across records, canonical count 0..4 and exact current native context. Recheck user/email/MFA/access/credential/factor and lifecycle revocation before decrypting or checking the code. Changes visible between issuance and verification refuse. Fingerprints compare current captured rows, not an unforgeable historical epoch for every possible restored field. Read the clock once while locked; admitted work crossing its deadline does not retroactively undo commit. Clock must leave room for a full 12-hour session within year 9999.

nodes.label: Native/source lifecycle and independent process acceptance
nodes.community_name: Internal enrolled TOTP login transaction and pending deployment gates
nodes.norm_label: native/source lifecycle and independent process acceptance
nodes.rationale: Acceptance uses actual TypeScript canonical control migrations, installed Better Auth crypto/cookie/session readers, synthetic users and independent native processes/connections. Prove native password→pending challenge→TOTP→persisted session→native/source cookie/session reads, no pre-MFA sessions, expiry/failure/lock/replay and scope/secret/credential/revocation refusals. Test lifecycle revocation after maximum-ROWID allocation, five failures, account locking across challenges, exact unlock boundary, failed SQL rollback, real commit-busy outcome, competing verifiers and writer fences in WAL/DELETE. Preserve source images on noncommitting refusal; inspect exact known committed effects and immutable audit triggers. Keep all existing checks green, review/fix concrete defects, and leave full R04/R41/server/clients/distribution/cutover open.

nodes.label: Password-rechecked native pending context and no provisional session
nodes.community_name: Internal enrolled TOTP login transaction and pending deployment gates
nodes.norm_label: password-rechecked native pending context and no provisional session
nodes.rationale: Begin uses the already verified password transaction: expensive KDF outside lock, exact current credential recheck inside BEGIN IMMEDIATE. Current verified email, active workspace access and enabled MFA are mandatory for a challenge. Exactly one verified twoFactor row must belong to the subject. Strict integer flags and bounded typed values fail closed; legacy NULL verified is not implicitly adopted. A current account lock refuses issuance. Write the source-compatible verification challenge and attempts rows, plus one native private context row, together; no temporary authenticated session is created. Native context binds the trusted workspace, current length-framed SHA256 credential/user/access fingerprint, MFA row/secret fingerprint and count of immutable credential/email/MFA/session-deletion lifecycle events (not MAX(id), so SQLite random ROWID allocation after the largest signed ID cannot hide revocation). These private verification fingerprints never enter audit, diagnostics or exported evidence. No native context means restart password login; foreign in-flight Better Auth challenges are not silently adopted.

nodes.label: Persistent native TOTP counter and atomic session commit
nodes.community_name: Internal enrolled TOTP login transaction and pending deployment gates
nodes.norm_label: persistent native totp counter and atomic session commit
nodes.rationale: A correct code must return a TOTP counter greater than the last native accepted counter for that factor row. Store its monotonic replay record in the existing verification table under a native namespace, together with failure reset, deletion of challenge/attempt/context, a fresh canonical 12-hour session and accepted telemetry. The existing immutable session_created trigger is the authoritative session lifecycle event. Valid TOTP alone grants nothing before successful commit. Return a signed session cookie only after known commit; company access still resolves the exact current session under the existing authorization fence. Concurrent verifies serialize so one challenge/code cannot create two sessions. Persistent replay protection is a native correction; it is not enforced by a legacy writer, and restore/lineage/cutover qualification remains separate.

nodes.label: Committed Rejected outcomes versus rollback and unknown commit
nodes.community_name: Internal enrolled TOTP login transaction and pending deployment gates
nodes.norm_label: committed rejected outcomes versus rollback and unknown commit
nodes.rationale: Known authentication refusals with committed attempt/audit effects are explicit Rejected outcomes, not rollback failures. Invalid context/admission and SQL errors return opaque fixed-code failures and explicitly roll back. Every commit error is OutcomeUnknown, retires the connection and withholds cookies; reconcile before retrying. Callback/SQL escape or external effects are not exposed by this use case. Existing connection preflight requires writable autocommit main, WAL/DELETE, FULL/EXTRA sync, foreign keys and no temp/attached schemas. Atomicity is one control DB only.

nodes.label: Workspace-bound random bearers and signed pending/session cookies
nodes.community_name: Internal enrolled TOTP login transaction and pending deployment gates
nodes.norm_label: workspace-bound random bearers and signed pending/session cookies
nodes.rationale: Runtime explicitly supplies workspace-bound cookie signer/verifier, MFA decryption keyring, trusted Clock and safe nonnegative audit-key version. Native bearer/row IDs use 32 OS-random bytes, canonical base64url; challenge identifiers prefix 2fa-. Signed cookies retain the installed Better Auth names and HMAC-SHA256 secret STRING/standard-base64/percent-encoding format. Secure profile emits Secure; both profiles emit Path=/, HttpOnly and SameSite=Lax. Challenge Max-Age 600 and session Max-Age 43200. Request verification retains bounded strict duplicate/secure-vs-development/service-header refusal. A session cookie never substitutes for the required signed MFA cookie. All bearer/cookie values omit Debug/Clone/Serde and owned new token/cookie buffers zeroize; broader input/library/compiler/allocator erasure is not claimed.

nodes.label: All-entry constant-time comparisons and zeroized serialization
nodes.community_name: Enrolled pending-MFA encrypted backup-code login contract
nodes.norm_label: all-entry constant-time comparisons and zeroized serialization
nodes.rationale: Compare all validated pool entries using fixed-length constant-time comparisons, without early match return. On a match, remove exactly that unique entry, serialize remaining codes in order and encrypt with a fresh nonce/current key. Owned parsed code buffers and serialized plaintext zeroize; wrappers do not expose Debug/Clone/Serde. Library parse internals, caller inputs and whole-operation constant-time execution are outside that claim. No plaintext code, pool, envelope, cookie or credential-derived fingerprint appears in persisted diagnostics or evidence.

nodes.label: Enrolled pending-MFA encrypted backup-code login contract
nodes.community_name: Enrolled pending-MFA encrypted backup-code login contract
nodes.norm_label: enrolled pending-mfa encrypted backup-code login contract
nodes.rationale: Extend the existing enrolled native password/pending-MFA transaction with backup-code verification as an alternative second factor. Require the same signed native challenge, trusted workspace/cookie/keyring/clock, canonical admitted control snapshot, current verified email/active access/verified MFA row and current credential/factor/lifecycle context. No password, service or session-cookie fallback and no session before the second factor. This scope is pending-login recovery, not enrollment, viewing/regenerating backup codes or recovery from a lost password.

nodes.label: Independent backup pool, race and cross-method acceptance
nodes.community_name: Enrolled pending-MFA encrypted backup-code login contract
nodes.norm_label: independent backup pool, race and cross-method acceptance
nodes.rationale: Acceptance uses actual canonical TypeScript migrations and configured backup-code generator/crypto/HTTP verifier, independent native WAL/DELETE processes, strict pool/code/lock/expiry/current-state tests, different-challenge same-code races, cross-method shared failure budgets and unchanged TOTP replay state. Verify exact pool removal/order/current-key re-encryption, session/cookie interoperability, full rollback and commit-busy with no cookie. Keep all existing checks green, preserve real company data, retain review/fix evidence and leave the full Rust epic open.

nodes.label: Locked current-pool CAS atomicity and unchanged TOTP replay
nodes.community_name: Enrolled pending-MFA encrypted backup-code login contract
nodes.norm_label: locked current-pool cas atomicity and unchanged totp replay
nodes.rationale: Under one control BEGIN IMMEDIATE, update the exact factor row with an old-ciphertext compare-and-set, reset account failure state, consume all pending challenge records, create the existing fresh twelve-hour session and append accepted recovery telemetry plus the immutable session-created trigger. Wrong codes and locked attempts use the distinct source endpoint two-factor-verify-backup-code in audit. Backup success does not create, reset or advance the TOTP replay record. Concurrent uses of the same code, even through different pending challenges, cannot create two sessions. Different still-current codes remain usable through other valid pending challenges; the pool is read from the locked current factor, not captured plaintext at issuance.

nodes.label: Rollback/unknown outcomes and source interoperability boundaries
nodes.community_name: Enrolled pending-MFA encrypted backup-code login contract
nodes.norm_label: rollback/unknown outcomes and source interoperability boundaries
nodes.rationale: Reuse existing operational rollback, known committed Rejected outcomes and OutcomeUnknown connection retirement: update/consumption/session/audit are atomic, cookie returned only after known commit, no automatic retry on uncertain commit. A late SQL fault after actual acceptance writes preserves original control state; a real DELETE-mode commit-busy withholds cookies. Successful native consumption remains readable by the installed source crypto and session reader, and the actual source HTTP backup-code verifier can consume a remaining native-reencrypted code on a separate synthetic database copy. This does not qualify live dual writers, restore lineage, physical opened-handle/lifetime admission, public endpoints, enrollment/regeneration or full identity parity.

nodes.label: Strict default encrypted code-pool shape and failure classes
nodes.community_name: Enrolled pending-MFA encrypted backup-code login contract
nodes.norm_label: strict default encrypted code-pool shape and failure classes
nodes.rationale: The installed configured Better Auth profile stores an encrypted JSON array of ten default backup codes; consumed pools contain zero to ten codes. Each code is exactly five ASCII alphanumeric characters, a hyphen and five ASCII alphanumeric characters, case-sensitive with no trimming or normalization. Accept bounded JSON whitespace/escapes, but refuse malformed JSON, wrong shapes/types, duplicate entries, more than ten entries or nondefault code profiles as unsupported stored state. Use the existing injected MFA keyring and authenticated current/historical envelope handling; no environment lookup or key guessing. A malformed encrypted pool is an operational refusal with no spent attempts. A valid empty pool or absent/malformed submitted code is an authentication failure with the existing shared five-attempt challenge and ten-failure/fifteen-minute account lock budgets.

nodes.label: Atomic enable/revoke/session/replay and committed one-time disclosure
nodes.community_name: Password-bound internal enrollment ceremony and source correction
nodes.norm_label: atomic enable/revoke/session/replay and committed one-time disclosure
nodes.rationale: On success, mark the exact factor verified, set user.twoFactorEnabled and canonical updatedAt, let the existing trigger record mfa_enabled and delete all pre-enrollment sessions, record the accepted TOTP counter, consume the setup challenge, reset account budgets, create a fresh twelve-hour session and append verification telemetry. All factor/user/session/replay/challenge/trigger/audit effects are one transaction. Create the fresh session after trigger revocation. Return its signed cookie and the exact ten backup codes only after known commit. A consumed challenge cannot disclose codes again. The legacy trigger actor system:better-auth is retained as a compatibility label and does not identify the executing runtime; accepted setup-start telemetry does not assert completed MFA.

nodes.label: Fresh unbiased enrollment secret/code pool and zeroized owned buffers
nodes.community_name: Password-bound internal enrollment ceremony and source correction
nodes.norm_label: fresh unbiased enrollment secret/code pool and zeroized owned buffers
nodes.rationale: Generate a fresh32-character source-profile TOTP secret, encrypt it and a fresh unique ten-code default backup pool with the configured current key/OS nonces. Backup codes use the existing five-alphanumeric/hyphen/five-alphanumeric format and unbiased OS entropy with bounded rejection sampling. Sensitive owned strings/buffers/URI/code lists omit Debug/Clone/Serde and zeroize; caller/compiler/allocator/library/OS copies and whole-operation constant-time behavior are not claimed. Backup codes remain encrypted and are withheld at begin.

nodes.community_name: Password-bound internal enrollment ceremony and source correction
nodes.norm_label: independent enrollment/source/process acceptance and pending gates
nodes.rationale: Acceptance: actual canonical TypeScript migrations, installed source crypto/URI/session/backup reader and independent WAL/DELETE native processes. Verify begin has no session/MFA-enabled events/codes; URI secret/labels/default OTP profile and final encrypted rows match the configured source. Test correct confirm, cross-ceremony/cross-method refusal, exact one-time code disclosure, source/native TOTP and backup login afterwards, old-session revocation, preserved budgets/restart/lock boundaries, changed identity/factor/pool/context, simultaneous begins/confirms, full late rollback and real commit-busy withholding. Keep all prior checks green and retain review/fix evidence. No real user/company data, public endpoint, backup-code management, password reset, physical opened-handle/lifetime admission, live dual writers, restore lineage, distribution or cutover is qualified; the full Rust epic remains open.

nodes.community_name: Password-bound internal enrollment ceremony and source correction
nodes.norm_label: locked confirmation budgets and current-state admission

Five wrong attempts burn the ceremony; ten consecutive account failures across restarts lock for fifteen minutes. Reuse the existing strict expiry, counter, lock, duplicate, canonical current-schema/history/integrity and ordered-event exhaustion guards. Operational crypto/pool/SQL failures roll back without spending attempts; known wrong-code/locked rejections commit declared counters/telemetry. Require a valid current ten-code pool before successful disclosure.

nodes.label: Password-bound internal enrollment ceremony and source correction
nodes.community_name: Password-bound internal enrollment ceremony and source correction
nodes.norm_label: password-bound internal enrollment ceremony and source correction
nodes.rationale: Provide an internal two-phase enrollment for an existing email-verified active workspace user with MFA disabled. Begin executes the existing password snapshot/KDF/locked-current-recheck operation and refuses enrolled users. It issues a private signed pending cookie and a source-compatible otpauth URI only after known commit, with no provisional authenticated session. Trusted runtime supplies cookie/keyring/clock/audit context and bounded issuer label; the account label comes from the locked canonical credential email, not a caller identity claim. This is a deliberate correction to source enrollment, which uses an existing session and reveals backup codes at enable time.

nodes.label: Full rollback, unknown commit and lost-response recovery boundary
nodes.community_name: Password-bound internal enrollment ceremony and source correction
nodes.norm_label: full rollback, unknown commit and lost-response recovery boundary
nodes.rationale: A late SQL failure after actual success writes must restore old sessions, old factor/user flags, pending challenge, backup ciphertext and all trigger/replay/audit state. Every commit error reports OutcomeUnknown, retires the connection and withholds URI/cookie/codes; do not claim rollback or retry automatically. Lost begin responses can be recovered by another password-verified restart. Lost/unknown confirmation requires reconciliation and, if MFA completed, normal TOTP login; it grants no code re-disclosure or regeneration shortcut.

nodes.community_name: Password-bound internal enrollment ceremony and source correction
nodes.norm_label: strict unverified-factor restart and isolated ceremony namespace
nodes.rationale: Store exactly one factor row with verified=0. Existing setup may restart only when exactly one row has strict verified=0; preserve its account failure/lock fields and refuse a future lock. Never silently adopt verified=1, NULL, duplicate or malformed factor state. Concurrent starts serialize; the later committed replacement invalidates every older setup context without resetting account budgets. No native TOTP replay row may already exist for an unverified factor. Bind a distinct enrollment context namespace/domain to the trusted workspace, current credential/access fingerprint, factor ID/encrypted secret/encrypted backup pool and immutable relevant lifecycle count. Use the existing bounded ten-minute challenge/attempt record shape, with no source in-flight adoption. Enrollment confirmation resolves only this namespace and strict user-MFA-disabled/factor-unverified state. TOTP and backup login resolve only the enrolled namespace and state; neither may upgrade an enrollment automatically or use backup codes to finish setup.

nodes.norm_label: canonical workspace audit and deletion-trigger mfa invalidation
nodes.rationale: Every existing-row SignOut, List and revocation appends a distinct workspace_audit event (session_signed_out, session_listed, session_revoked, other_sessions_revoked, sessions_revoked), entity_type native_session_control_v1, entity_id canonical JSON [subject,currentSessionId,auditKeyVersion,targetIdOrNull,deletedCount], actor user:<subject>, created_at from sampled trusted time. nodes.community_name: Own-session control runtime proof and single-lock admission
nodes.norm_label: fresh current-factor admission without local credentials and own-id revocation
nodes.rationale: List and revocation require exact current-token resolution, canonical unexpired twelve-hour-bounded session younger than ten minutes, current verified-email/MFA-enabled user, active member/owner workspace access and exactly one factor with strict verified=1. Do not require a local credential account, decrypt MFA data or refresh session age. No company privilege or target bearer is required. RevokeOne accepts a bounded nonempty non-control session ID and deletes only WHERE id/subject match; missing and foreign IDs have the same successful zero-deletion result. RevokeAll deletes all own rows, including current and expired; RevokeOthers atomically deletes every own row except current, including expired. These intentionally strengthen source authoritative-session-only revocation with freshness/current workspace/MFA gates, replace source bearer targets and make source active-only multi-delete others atomic and inclusive. No other user's session may be listed or deleted.

nodes.label: Own-session control runtime proof and single-lock admission
nodes.community_name: Own-session control runtime proof and single-lock admission
nodes.norm_label: own-session control runtime proof and single-lock admission
nodes.rationale: Implement internal List, SignOut, RevokeOne(sessionId), RevokeOthers and RevokeAll operations on an admitted control connection. Runtime injects only CookieVerifier, Clock and bounded audit key version, without requiring an MFA encryption keyring or password. Preflight connection readiness before any reusable refusal; accept only a session-kind proof from the same workspace, signer key and configured cookie profile. Service/pending proof and caller subject claims do not authorize these operations. All final observations, deletions, lifecycle triggers and accepted audit hold one BEGIN IMMEDIATE and one sampled trusted Clock. Canonical current control schema/history/integrity and ordered-event exhaustion guards remain mandatory.

nodes.label: Rollback, unknown commit and current-session reconciliation
nodes.community_name: Own-session control runtime proof and single-lock admission
nodes.norm_label: rollback, unknown commit and current-session reconciliation
nodes.rationale: Known operational/validation failures roll back all writes and release no result/headers; confirmed rollback plus postflight determines handle reuse. Every commit error returns OutcomeUnknown, retires the handle and releases no listing/receipt/clear headers, without automatic retry or rollback assertion. The independent pure local-clear helper is not evidence of server deletion. Reconcile lost/unknown results by current token/session inspection, never by resurrecting rows or accepting cached provider responses. Revocation may not race past another admitted writer lock or resurrect deleted sessions. Repeated SignOut with an already-deleted valid proof is a no-op success; other operations need a still-current authorized session.

nodes.label: Source/native session process acceptance and pending gates
nodes.community_name: Own-session control runtime proof and single-lock admission
nodes.norm_label: source/native session process acceptance and pending gates
nodes.rationale: Acceptance uses actual canonical migrations, installed source session readers/logout/revocation/cookie attributes on separate synthetic copies, and independent native WAL/DELETE processes. Cover token-free stable bounded listing, no local credential requirement, nullable/display metadata, fresh/expiry/current-state/proof/target refusals, expired/disabled/malformed-time/missing logout, foreign-user protection, exact trigger/audit counts, pending MFA invalidation after real deletion, contention/revoke races and no new-session resurrection, complete late rollback, real DELETE commit-busy withholding and source/native interoperable revocation. Preserve all previous checks. No exposed HTTP/CLI/MCP/UI endpoint, physical SQLite-handle/workspace lifetime admission, source/live dual writers, restore lineage, remote OAuth/provider/cache/trusted-device flows, real data adoption, distribution/cutover or whole Rust epic completion is qualified.

nodes.label: Timestamp/access-independent exact-token logout and independent local clear
nodes.community_name: Own-session control runtime proof and single-lock admission
nodes.norm_label: timestamp/access-independent exact-token logout and independent local clear
nodes.rationale: SignOut uses only runtime-bound proof and exact token row lookup/deletion, without expiry/freshness/access/MFA/factor/password gates. It handles expired or malformed timestamp cells and disabled users. Structural ID/subject ambiguity still refuses. Already missing rows return known-commit idempotent success without fabricated subject/audit. Unlike source's swallowed DB errors, a database failure is never reported as confirmed server revocation. A pure runtime helper can independently expire configured native session_token/session_data/dont_remember/two_factor cookies without claiming database success. Transactional output carries these clear headers only after known commit when SignOut/RevokeAll or RevokeOne-current removes the caller; no headers/data on failed/unknown commit. Chunked cache/account/OAuth-provider logout remains unqualified; current native profile issues no such state and source cookie cache is disabled.

nodes.label: Token-free allowlisted stable list with total-row and metadata bounds
nodes.community_name: Own-session control runtime proof and single-lock admission
nodes.norm_label: token-free allowlisted stable list with total-row and metadata bounds
nodes.rationale: List is an audited writer operation. Validate at most1000 total own rows before filtering, failing explicitly at1001 rather than returning a partial list. Each ID is bounded4096 non-control/nonblank bytes; timestamps are canonical UTC millisecond, created<=now, expires>created and lifetime<=12h. Invalid owned timestamps refuse even in expired rows. Return only active rows, sorted createdAt descending then ID bytewise ascending, with allowlisted id/createdAt/expiresAt/current/ipAddress/userAgent. IP and user-agent are nullable bounded non-control display strings (256/2048 bytes), never identity/authority. Bound total returned metadata to1MiB, never include tokens or arbitrary row fields. Revocation remains available for cleanup of an oversized/malformed listing. Source's token-bearing/unbounded listing is a deliberate native versioned contract correction, not a byte-compatible source response claim.

nodes.label: Atomic credential/link/session/lifecycle recovery audit and secret hygiene
nodes.community_name: Source reset bearer as sole recovery authority
nodes.norm_label: atomic credential/link/session/lifecycle recovery audit and secret hygiene
nodes.rationale: One writer transaction contains credential mutation/creation, all link consumption, all session deletion and its canonical session_deleted/credential_updated triggers, native workspace audit and accepted reset-password telemetry. The workspace_audit event is password_reset_completed / native_password_reset_v1, actor user:<subject>, with a JSON tuple of subject, audit-key version, credential-created boolean, deleted-session count and consumed-reset-row count. Telemetry includes only fixed endpoint/outcome, subject, version and trusted timestamp. Neither audit contains email, raw token, URL, hash, password, provider token or display metadata. Returned success is unit only after known commit. PasswordHash is zeroized on drop; identifiers built from the token are zeroized. Caller owns input and transport buffers.

nodes.label: Exact canonical credential ownership and bounded mutation or creation
nodes.community_name: Source reset bearer as sole recovery authority
nodes.norm_label: exact canonical credential ownership and bounded mutation or creation
nodes.rationale: The canonical credential key is (issuer='local:credential', accountId=subject). Its existing owner must be that subject and providerId must be 'credential'; a conflicting foreign owner/provider refuses without adopting or overwriting it. An existing credential retains ID, createdAt and all other provider fields while only password/updatedAt change. A missing canonical credential is created with fresh OS-random ID and exact local provider fields. Other provider accounts are untouched. A null/malformed old password does not prevent legitimate reset; no old password is verified. User, factor, backup codes, factor lock budget, replay state and membership rows are unchanged.

nodes.label: Documented source versioned reset corrections and profile limits
nodes.community_name: Source reset bearer as sole recovery authority
nodes.norm_label: documented source versioned reset corrections and profile limits
nodes.rationale: The installed source consumes its latest matching row (and all duplicate identifiers) before KDF and subsequent mutations, accepts expiry equality, deletes expired values while refusing, and leaves sibling reset links valid. Native deliberately strengthens this into one atomic transaction, refuses duplicate/malformed/oversized-lifetime records, uses strict expiry and revokes sibling links. These are documented versioned corrections rather than byte-for-byte endpoint parity. Current source has no secondary verification storage or identifier hashing configured. Different configured token lifetimes/storage/identifier formats require separate qualification.

nodes.label: NotCommitted and unknown commit with explicit reconciliation
nodes.community_name: Source reset bearer as sole recovery authority
nodes.norm_label: notcommitted and unknown commit with explicit reconciliation
nodes.rationale: A pre-commit error explicitly rolls back and reports NotCommitted with connection reuse only after successful rollback and readiness check. Any commit error reports OutcomeUnknown, retires the handle and withholds success. Observing an old image after closing a busy test connection does not strengthen that guarantee into universal rollback. Do not automatically replay an uncertain reset or promise the client its old password is still valid; reconcile current state or initiate a new recovery through the eventual delivery flow. This increment sends no external effects and exposes no endpoint.

nodes.label: Own sibling reset/session revocation and pending-context limits
nodes.community_name: Source reset bearer as sole recovery authority
nodes.norm_label: own sibling reset/session revocation and pending-context limits
nodes.rationale: Success deletes every `reset-password:` verification row whose value is this exact subject, including outstanding sibling links, and all this subject's session rows, including expired/malformed-time rows. Other subjects and verification namespaces are preserved. A user cannot reuse an older recovery link after native recovery. Native pending MFA/enrollment context remains stored but its credential fingerprint and actual credential_updated/session_deleted lifecycle observations make prior context unusable where such a credential context existed. Credential insertion has no canonical credential_updated trigger and no such event is fabricated. No claim is made that source in-flight two-factor/trusted-device flows are fully revoked by this implementation.

nodes.label: Source-issued reset completion independent acceptance
nodes.community_name: Source reset bearer as sole recovery authority
nodes.rationale: Acceptance uses synthetic canonical current control copies in WAL/DELETE, actual installed source request token issuance with an in-memory email sink, source/native hash and login readers, existing and absent canonical credentials, foreign provider/owner boundaries, original UTF-16 length/NFKC, strict token/time/schema/config refusals, preserved access/MFA state, one-time/sibling consumption, full rollback, separate-process writer contention, unlocked-KDF token deletion and real commit-busy at creation/update. Full native and Rust integration regression, scoped GDD readiness and read-only review bind evidence to actual source hashes. No real company/user data, production mail or deployment is involved.

nodes.label: Source reset bearer as sole recovery authority
nodes.community_name: Source reset bearer as sole recovery authority
nodes.norm_label: source reset bearer as sole recovery authority
nodes.rationale: `password_reset::execute` completes an existing Better Auth 1.7.1 `reset-password:<token>` record on the caller's admitted current control connection. Its only recovery authority is possession of the exact current bearer and its unique unexpired database row. It accepts no requested subject, account ID, membership claim, session or MFA proof. The runtime injects Clock and audit-key version. Actual physical handle/workspace lifetime admission and public origin/rate/bounded-blocking dispatch remain prerequisites before exposing it. It issues no reset link, sends no mail, redirects nowhere and grants no session or cookie.

nodes.label: Strict source token grammar and original UTF16 password policy
nodes.community_name: Source reset bearer as sole recovery authority
nodes.norm_label: strict source token grammar and original utf16 password policy
nodes.rationale: Preflight rejects an unready connection before input/KDF work. Token grammar is exactly the source generator's 24 ASCII alphanumeric characters, case-sensitive, without trimming/percent decoding. The original password must contain 12–128 UTF-16 code units, before shared NFKC/scrypt derivation; spaces are preserved. Six supplementary scalars count as twelve code units. Rust strings cannot represent isolated JavaScript surrogates; those are outside this native input contract. Shared crypto budgets and OS entropy apply. No request-derived subject or pre-KDF database snapshot authorizes later changes.

nodes.label: Unique current reset row strict lifetime and access-independent recovery
nodes.community_name: Source reset bearer as sole recovery authority
nodes.norm_label: unique current reset row strict lifetime and access-independent recovery
nodes.rationale: Exactly one verification row must match the complete identifier under binary comparison. Missing tokens or missing referenced users refuse opaquely. Duplicate identifiers, malformed/nonblank/control/4096-byte-bounded row IDs or subjects, noncanonical UTC timestamps, createdAt > updatedAt, updatedAt > now, expiresAt <= createdAt, or a lifetime over one hour refuse. Native expiry is strict: expiresAt must be greater than now. Rejected operations do not delete expired or ambiguous rows; confirmed rollback preserves them. A reset is allowed for an existing disabled, unverified, nonmember or MFA-disabled user, without old-password or MFA-keyring dependency; this never changes access or verification state.

nodes.label: Unlocked salted hashing then trusted-clock current writer resolution
nodes.community_name: Source reset bearer as sole recovery authority
nodes.norm_label: unlocked salted hashing then trusted-clock current writer resolution
nodes.rationale: The new salted hash is derived with no SQLite transaction or writer held, including for syntactically valid but absent tokens. Only afterward does BEGIN IMMEDIATE acquire the one admitted writer. One trusted clock sample supplies expiry decisions and canonical millisecond UTC mutation/audit timestamps; accepted range is 0 through 253402300799999. The audit-key version is a nonnegative JavaScript-safe integer. The writer admits exact current schema/history and resolves the token anew, so deletion or successful consumption during unlocked KDF cannot be bypassed.

nodes.label: Known/unknown confidential HMAC request audit
nodes.community_name: Internal reset request mail handoff and callback contract
nodes.rationale: Both known and unknown paths commit a native_reset_request_v1 workspace_audit/password_reset_requested event, actor system:auth-recovery, whose JSON tuple is HMAC identity, audit-key version and optional subject. The HMAC exactly matches rentemester-auth-audit-v1 plus NUL and the canonical email with the configured secret's string bytes. Canonical request-password-reset telemetry records attempted, optional subject, HMAC/version and the same trusted timestamp; attempted never claims mail delivery. No audit contains raw email, bearer, URL, password, credential hash or transport error. User/account/factor/access/session/lifecycle state is preserved by request issuance.

nodes.label: Documented request sender/URL/expiry/cleanup source corrections
nodes.community_name: Internal reset request mail handoff and callback contract
nodes.rationale: Installed Better Auth 1.7.1 request normalizes only lowercase, emits the same normal acknowledgement for unknown email, retains sibling links and constructs the same URL. Its runInBackgroundOrAwait catches sender rejection, so a disabled/failing sender can still leave a persisted link and appear successful. Native documents and reports internal committed delivery uncertainty instead of claiming a rollback or silent delivery. Native also refuses insecure/nonexplicit URL configuration and malformed/duplicate/expired-at-equality preview records, and avoids source's unrelated verification cleanup. These are explicit source corrections. Actual HTTP request-origin/CSRF admission is distinct from validating a redirect and is not implemented here.

nodes.label: Injected bounded sensitive mail port and opaque external errors
nodes.community_name: Internal reset request mail handoff and callback contract
nodes.norm_label: injected bounded sensitive mail port and opaque external errors
nodes.rationale: The runtime injects a CookieVerifier solely for the existing domain-separated HMAC audit identity, a Clock, RecoveryLinks configuration and JavaScript-safe audit-key version. No signer/session proof grants recovery authority. A ResetSender is a real external boundary: enabled() must reflect already validated transport configuration, and send() accepts only a private-field sensitive ResetMessage with recipient/token/action URL accessors. Its failure is opaque DeliveryUnconfirmed, never raw provider errors. DisabledResetSender refuses by default. Trusted adapters must enforce finite network deadlines, bounded same-message retries and no secret logging. Request issuance never retries by manufacturing another token. Unit output contains no bearer or account-existence field.

nodes.label: Internal reset request mail handoff and callback contract
nodes.community_name: Internal reset request mail handoff and callback contract
nodes.norm_label: internal reset request mail handoff and callback contract
nodes.rationale: `reset_request::execute` issues a source-compatible recovery link and hands it to a trusted injected mail port only after a known database commit. `reset_request::callback` previews the allowed redirect without consuming a token. Together with existing native reset completion this covers the internal request/link/preview/completion sequence. Public HTTP acknowledgement/CSRF/rate/bounded-blocking dispatch, a concrete Rust HTTP mail adapter, durable delivery/outbox, actual physical control/workspace lifetime admission and deployment remain pending. No production mail is sent by this increment.

nodes.label: Nonconsuming current-token stable callback snapshot
nodes.community_name: Internal reset request mail handoff and callback contract
nodes.rationale: Callback runs one admitted stable deferred read snapshot with one trusted Clock sample and no writes. It reuses completion's exact token grammar/current unique-row/existing-user/canonical-time/one-hour-lifetime/strict-expiry rules. Missing or expired tokens yield INVALID_TOKEN redirects; duplicate/malformed control records refuse opaquely. The same token can be previewed repeatedly without consumption or general cleanup. Valid preview is not a reservation, authenticated session or promise that subsequent completion succeeds. Final completion always resolves under its own writer.

nodes.label: Pinned parsed-origin recovery link configuration and redirect policy
nodes.community_name: Internal reset request mail handoff and callback contract
nodes.norm_label: pinned parsed-origin recovery link configuration and redirect policy
nodes.rationale: RecoveryLinks uses pinned url 2.5.8 and real parsed-origin equality, never string-prefix matching or a request-derived Host. Config accepts 1–32 explicit HTTP(S) origin entries without path/query/fragment/nonempty credentials/wildcard hosts. Base origin must occur in the explicit list. Secure mode requires HTTPS; Development permits HTTP only for localhost, 127.0.0.1 or ::1. Root-relative destinations follow the source's restricted ASCII path/query grammar, reject authority/backslash and case-insensitive encoded initial slash/backslash, and resolve against the injected base. Absolute destinations must have an allowed parsed origin and no nonempty credentials/backslashes/controls. Relative fragments are rejected; allowed absolute fragments and query values are preserved. All raw URL inputs are bounded to 4096 bytes.

nodes.label: Postcommit mail external-effect uncertainty and nonenumerating mapper obligation
nodes.community_name: Internal reset request mail handoff and callback contract
nodes.norm_label: postcommit mail external-effect uncertainty and nonenumerating mapper obligation
nodes.rationale: All issuance/audit effects commit together before the port is called, with no SQLite transaction or writer held during mail. A known commit may be followed by another writer consuming/revoking the link before mail; a successful send does not reserve or reauthorize it. After confirmed rollback, failure is NotCommitted and the port has not run. Any commit error is OutcomeUnknown, retires the connection and never calls mail. A mail error after known commit is a distinct internal Committed/auth_delivery_unconfirmed failure: the reset row and audit exist and may remain usable. Timeout/failure cannot prove that no email was delivered. Do not return NotCommitted, delete a possibly delivered token or automatically reissue/replay an uncertain request. Unit success means the known recipient's port confirmed the handoff, or an unknown email was generically acknowledged, not guaranteed end-user delivery. The future public mapper must conceal committed delivery/existence differences and keep the same acknowledgement for known/unknown addresses; exposing these internal states directly would enumerate accounts.

nodes.label: Source-compatible query replacement and committed sensitive redirect result
nodes.community_name: Internal reset request mail handoff and callback contract
nodes.norm_label: source-compatible query replacement and committed sensitive redirect result
nodes.rationale: Callback revalidates the destination. A valid row and nonempty allowed callback set its token query parameter; an absent/expired row sets error=INVALID_TOKEN. Query replacement follows URLSearchParams.set, preserving the first matching parameter's position and removing duplicate occurrences, while retaining unrelated parameters and an absolute fragment. Missing/empty callback uses <origin>/api/auth/error?error=INVALID_TOKEN. The sensitive URL is returned only after the read transaction has ended successfully. Caller owns transport/input buffers; bearer and final message/redirect URL wrappers have no Debug/Clone/Serde exposure and zeroize their owned strings. Parser intermediates are not claimed universally zeroized.

nodes.label: Preflight email/redirect validation and unbiased source bearer generation
nodes.community_name: Internal reset request mail handoff and callback contract
nodes.norm_label: preflight email/redirect validation and unbiased source bearer generation
nodes.rationale: Preflight rejects an unready handle first. A disabled sender refuses before identity lookup for both known and unknown emails. Input uses the existing bounded ASCII practical-email grammar and lowercase-without-trimming correction. Redirect and injected configuration are validated before durable effects. A fresh source-format 24-character alphanumeric bearer uses unbiased rejection sampling from OS bytes; generation has a finite entropy-attempt bound and secrets are zeroized. A separate OS-random row ID is generated. Neither subject nor token identity is request-injected. A valid-looking but absent email still generates the unused bearer and follows the writer/audit path; no constant-time or constant-I/O claim is made.

nodes.label: Source-backed request/callback independent acceptance
nodes.community_name: Internal reset request mail handoff and callback contract
nodes.rationale: Acceptance uses synthetic current control fixtures and separate WAL/DELETE processes, real installed source callback and reset completion on native-issued links, source mail-link encoding and observed swallowed sender rejection, trusted-origin/Unicode/encoding/configuration cases, HMAC audit parity, unknown-email/no-cleanup preservation, disabled/unconfirmed ports, no-lock post-commit handoff, contention, late rollback and real commit-busy with no mail. Existing MFA/reset/session regression, full Rust checks, runtime typecheck/lint, actual scoped GDD structural readiness and read-only review bind evidence to final source hashes. No real user/company migration, external mail or production operation occurs.

nodes.label: Source-compatible encoded mail URL and atomic reset issuance
nodes.community_name: Internal reset request mail handoff and callback contract
nodes.norm_label: source-compatible encoded mail url and atomic reset issuance
nodes.rationale: The exact message URL is <origin>/api/auth/reset-password/<token>?callbackURL=<JavaScript encodeURIComponent of the original optional redirect>. Omitted/empty redirect produces callbackURL=. Component escaping preserves JavaScript's unescaped !~*'() and uses %20 for spaces, not form-style +. Only the persisted matched user's exact canonical email receives the message. The use case acquires BEGIN IMMEDIATE, admits current canonical schema/history, samples the Clock once and resolves an existing user by canonical exact email. No password, credential, emailVerified, MFA or workspace-access condition excludes recovery, and none of those states is changed. Known email inserts one unique-checked reset-password:<token> row containing subject and canonical createdAt=updatedAt=now, expiresAt=now+one hour. Accepted issuance clocks range from 0 through 253402297199999. Unknown email inserts no reset row and sends nothing; unrelated expired verification rows are never globally cleaned up. Older links survive a request and are invalidated by the already-specified successful native completion.

nodes.label: Pinned URL dependency reference and unqualified supply-chain scope
nodes.community_name: Internal reset request mail handoff and callback contract
nodes.norm_label: pinned url dependency reference and unqualified supply-chain scope
nodes.rationale: URL dependency reference: https://docs.rs/url/2.5.8/url/struct.Url.html (parsed origin, join and query operations); the Cargo lock records the concrete transitive dependency graph. This does not qualify whole-platform supply-chain/distribution acceptance.

nodes.label: Bounded message parsing without action authority
nodes.community_name: Concrete HTTP JSON auth-mail handoff contract
nodes.norm_label: bounded message parsing without action authority
nodes.rationale: Recipient is nonblank, control-free, at most 4096 bytes and satisfies the practical email grammar without trimming. Token is nonblank/control-free and at most 8192 bytes; generic mail supports existing verification/invitation token formats, while ResetSender receives the already validated native 24-alnum reset message. Action URL is bounded to 16384 bytes, parsed HTTP(S), has a host and excludes nonempty credentials/backslash/controls. Final serialized JSON must not exceed 32768 bytes. These are delivery-input checks, not authorization of an email, invitation or recovery action; the relevant use case must validate the subject/action before constructing a message.

nodes.label: Concrete HTTP JSON auth-mail handoff contract
nodes.community_name: Concrete HTTP JSON auth-mail handoff contract
nodes.norm_label: concrete http json auth-mail handoff contract
nodes.rationale: HttpJsonAuthSender implements the existing ResetSender and exposes one explicit MailKind (verification/password-reset/workspace-invitation) delivery operation for the existing auth-mail gateway. It is a concrete blocking HTTPS client, with no database or background delivery queue. Reset requests call this port only after their separately verified known commit. A successful transport result confirms gateway handoff, not end-user receipt, and a failed result can follow actual acceptance. Existing reset-request Committed/auth_delivery_unconfirmed semantics and future public acknowledgement concealment remain binding.

nodes.label: Contained gateway-only HTTP policy without forwarding
nodes.community_name: Concrete HTTP JSON auth-mail handoff contract
nodes.norm_label: contained gateway-only http policy without forwarding
nodes.rationale: The client is HTTPS-only, HTTP/1, with redirects, automatic referrer, proxies (including environment/system proxy), cookies, decompression, verbose wire logging, TLS key logging and reqwest-internal protocol retries disabled. It allows at most 64 HTTP/1 response headers; the HTTP dependency's bounded parser buffers remain in force. Only the response status is inspected, and the body is dropped without parsing, logging or draining an unbounded response. No action URL is fetched: only the configured gateway endpoint receives a POST. Redirects never forward credentials or mail content, even within the same origin. Supporting a required proxy, private roots or HTTP/2-only gateway needs a separately specified configuration, not an implicit fallback.

nodes.label: Explicit native transport/source corrections
nodes.community_name: Concrete HTTP JSON auth-mail handoff contract
nodes.rationale: The source gateway has the same normal wire/templates/HMAC, three-attempt network/429/5xx behavior and eight-second wall-clock budget. Native intentionally uses a monotonic budget, explicit parser/input bounds, stricter endpoint query/credential restrictions, prepared fail-closed async DNS, pinned roots, disabled redirects/proxies/keylogging and no hidden retries. These are documented source corrections. Existing source runInBackgroundOrAwait may swallow a sender rejection; native transport returns uncertainty to the use case, whose failure/public acknowledgement rules are separate.

nodes.label: Explicit Unicode-capable private gateway configuration
nodes.community_name: Concrete HTTP JSON auth-mail handoff contract
nodes.rationale: GatewayConfig is injected operator configuration: HTTPS endpoint, bearer token, from address and HMAC idempotency secret, with no environment secret/host/proxy fallback. Configuration/sender/message types expose no Debug/Clone/Serde secrets. Endpoint is at most 4096 bytes and excludes query, fragment, nonempty credentials, backslashes, wildcard host and controls. Bearer is nonblank trimmed ASCII, at most 4096 bytes, and must form a valid header; its HeaderValue is marked sensitive. Original from input is bounded to 4096 bytes, trimmed for the outgoing payload and checked against the source practical non-whitespace one-at/dotted-domain grammar. Valid Unicode addresses remain supported. Idempotency secret is nonblank, control-free and at most 4096 bytes; original UTF-8 bytes, including internal spaces/non-ASCII, are retained.

nodes.label: Monotonic eight-second same-message three-attempt budget
nodes.community_name: Concrete HTTP JSON auth-mail handoff contract
nodes.rationale: Delivery starts one monotonic Instant budget of eight seconds before input/serialization work. Each of at most three attempts gets only the remaining timeout. Any 2xx before budget expiry acknowledges handoff; 429 and 500–599 permit retry, other HTTP statuses stop immediately, and transport/TLS/DNS errors permit bounded retry. Backoff is 100ms then 200ms, clipped to remaining budget; it does not honor Retry-After or generate another message/token. The same body/key are retained throughout. No attempt starts after exhausted budget. Timed-out DNS or response futures are canceled by the client request timeout. Scheduling delays, synchronous system configuration/client construction, client destruction's runtime-thread join and whole-server worker admission are outside this ordinary-scheduling delivery budget; this is not a hard realtime or universal process-shutdown guarantee.

nodes.label: Opaque delivery uncertainty and secret/privacy boundaries
nodes.community_name: Concrete HTTP JSON auth-mail handoff contract
nodes.norm_label: opaque delivery uncertainty and secret/privacy boundaries
nodes.rationale: Failure is the fixed opaque DeliveryUnconfirmed only. Raw transport/provider errors, response bodies, addresses, endpoint paths, tokens, URLs, headers and keys are not added to errors or logs by this module. It installs no logger. Authorization headers are sensitive and owned HMAC key/body buffers are zeroized; reqwest/TLS/URL/header/body copies and caller inputs are not universally zeroized. Application-wide dependency tracing and platform crash/storage qualification remain release gates. Gateway acceptance is not proof of final delivery, revocation, database rollback or safe automatic new-token retry.

nodes.label: Pinned TLS roots and explicit platform trust limits
nodes.community_name: Concrete HTTP JSON auth-mail handoff contract
nodes.norm_label: pinned tls roots and explicit platform trust limits
nodes.rationale: TLS uses reqwest 0.13.5/rustls and the pinned Mozilla webpki-root-certs 1.0.9 roots with certificate and hostname validation. Explicit roots bypass the platform certificate verifier and its possible synchronous OS/network work. Production offers no invalid-certificate/name bypass or test-root injection. Private/OS-added trust roots, OS revocation policies, root-store maintenance, other TLS backends and platform qualification need explicit release/deployment decisions; bundled roots do not update without a new build. The ignored synthetic process helper alone can substitute an ephemeral local CA and DNS server, using the same validated client policy and delivery code.

nodes.label: Prepared fail-closed async DNS without lazy public fallback
nodes.community_name: Concrete HTTP JSON auth-mail handoff contract
nodes.norm_label: prepared fail-closed async dns without lazy public fallback
nodes.rationale: Construction validates configuration and creates the reusable client. Domain endpoints load the system DNS configuration once at construction using direct pinned Hickory; configuration acquisition errors fail InvalidConfig. Hickory also loads the hosts file at construction on a best-effort basis, substituting empty hosts if that read fails. IP endpoints need no resolver. The custom async resolver uses only that prepared configuration, without lazy system lookups, getaddrinfo or implicit public-resolver fallback. This specifically corrects reqwest's default Hickory lazy initializer, which could block on system configuration and fall back to Google DNS. Configuration/hosts acquisition and client startup are outside the delivery-time budget. Changes to system DNS configuration require rebuilding the configured sender.

nodes.label: Pinned transport source/API references
nodes.community_name: Concrete HTTP JSON auth-mail handoff contract
nodes.rationale: Primary API/source references: https://docs.rs/reqwest/0.13.5/reqwest/blocking/struct.ClientBuilder.html and the exact Cargo.lock dependency sources (reqwest blocking client/DNS resolver, Hickory resolver/provider and TLS root branch). Local source oracle: src/server/auth-email.ts and tests/unit/auth-email-http-json-v1.test.ts.

nodes.label: Real loopback TLS/DNS and independent wire-oracle acceptance
nodes.community_name: Concrete HTTP JSON auth-mail handoff contract
nodes.norm_label: real loopback tls/dns and independent wire-oracle acceptance
nodes.rationale: Acceptance uses real ephemeral local CA/leaf TLS servers and a synthetic UDP DNS server, with the installed TypeScript sender as an in-memory independent body/header/HMAC oracle for all three kinds and Unicode input. Cases cover same-body/key retries and token separation, 2xx/4xx/429/5xx decisions, no redirect forwarding, environment proxy/keylog refusal, untrusted-root and hostname refusal, network disconnect attempts, genuinely stalled TLS-response and unanswered-DNS budgets, actual async hostname/SAN lookup, input/body limits and the concrete native ResetSender trait. All mock listeners bind loopback, private keys live only in temporary test files, and no external email/gateway is contacted. Full Rust regression, scoped GDD structural readiness, runtime typecheck/lint and independent review bind evidence to the exact final sources.

nodes.label: Three-kind exact wire templates and domain-separated HMAC
nodes.community_name: Concrete HTTP JSON auth-mail handoff contract
nodes.norm_label: three-kind exact wire templates and domain-separated hmac
nodes.rationale: One compact JSON request uses exactly version=rentemester-auth-email-v1, kind, to, from, subject, text and actionUrl. All three source Danish subject/text templates and kind values are preserved. The four explicit headers are authorization=Bearer <injected value>, content-type=application/json, idempotency-key=<lowercase hex HMAC-SHA256>, and x-rentemester-auth-event=<kind>; normal HTTP framing headers are supplied by the client. HMAC input is rentemester-auth-email-v1, NUL, kind, NUL, token using configured secret UTF-8 bytes, exactly as the source. Same-kind/same-token retries reuse both the serialized bytes and key; different tokens/kinds produce independently scoped keys. No raw token is added as a JSON field.

nodes.label: Owned bounded blocking permit through cancellation and postcommit mail
nodes.community_name: Native reset router with trusted injected admitted executor
nodes.norm_label: owned bounded blocking permit through cancellation and postcommit mail
nodes.rationale: At most4 admitted bodies/jobs share one non-waiting owned semaphore. Full capacity returns503 before body parsing/executor work; there is no unbounded application job queue. Body validation holds the permit. After validation, spawn_blocking owns it through the entire trusted executor, including its native transaction and postcommit mail. Dropping the HTTP future/JoinHandle or disconnecting does not free capacity while blocking work continues, cancel a started mutation, regenerate a token or establish rollback. Work may wait within Tokio's blocking pool; global pool/sockets/header-read admission and hard shutdown remain unqualified. No request timeout wraps a potentially committed operation and reports it as canceled.

nodes.label: Explicit same-origin/Host admission without forwarded authority
nodes.community_name: Native reset router with trusted injected admitted executor
nodes.norm_label: explicit same-origin/host admission without forwarded authority
nodes.rationale: Construction validates one explicit canonical origin through existing RecoveryLinks policy. Secure profile requires HTTPS; development HTTP permits only configured localhost/loopback. Request Origin and Host must each occur once and exactly equal the configured canonical origin/authority. Missing/null/duplicate/foreign Origin is refused even without cookies. Forwarded host/proto/IP headers never establish authority or a rate identity. If present, Sec-Fetch-Site must be same-origin, same-site or none. This same-origin route has no cross-origin CORS grant. Trusted redirects are separately validated using RecoveryLinks against that one configured origin; relative valid destinations remain allowed. It does not derive deployment configuration from request headers.

nodes.label: Real-socket/native/source acceptance and documented corrections
nodes.community_name: Native reset router with trusted injected admitted executor
nodes.rationale: Acceptance combines real socket tests (ACK/rate spoofing, host/origin/media/JSON refusal, content-length/chunked limit, stalled body deadline, route limits), atomic concurrent rate/capacity/window tests and cancellation-held blocking permits. A separate20-case process suite starts the Rust router with a synthetic executor that calls the real native reset_request::execute under WAL and DELETE: known/unknown/mail-failure ACKs match an actual installed BetterAuth handler; link/audit effects, rollback and unchanged users are inspected; mail asserts independent connection visibility and no SQLite writer is held. Hostile Origin has no native effect. Source special rate rule is3/60 with lastRequest updates and IPv6 /64 normalization. Source cookie-free Origin permissiveness, loose media matching and unknown-field stripping are deliberately tightened. Source mail errors are swallowed after persistence; native preserves explicit internal commit/delivery uncertainty and conceals it here.

nodes.label: Socket-peer process-local bounded rate policy
nodes.community_name: Native reset router with trusted injected admitted executor
nodes.rationale: Rate admission uses only Axum ConnectInfo populated from the actual accepted SocketAddr, never raw client headers. Missing peer refuses. IPv4-mapped IPv6 normalizes to IPv4; native IPv6 shares its /64 prefix. An atomic mutex protects at most4096 in-memory IP buckets. Each bucket admits at most3 requests until60 seconds after the last admitted request; admitted calls update lastRequest, refused calls do not. Expired buckets are removed before admission. Full map or rate denial returns429 with fixed Retry-After60, independent of email/existence. Invalid JSON also consumes rate admission. Origin/media admission happens first. This process-local bounded implementation deliberately does not claim source database persistence, restart resistance, multi-process limits or trusted-proxy client identity. A proxy currently shares its socket peer bucket. Those are production/release admission gates, not an excuse to trust arbitrary forwarded headers.

nodes.label: Strict JSON/media/redirect admission and bounded body deadline
nodes.community_name: Native reset router with trusted injected admitted executor
nodes.norm_label: strict json/media/redirect admission and bounded body deadline
nodes.rationale: Only application/json with optional charset=utf-8 parameters is accepted, case-insensitively; duplicate Content-Type and every Content-Encoding are refused. Query parameters on this route are refused. Strict JSON has required string email and optional string redirectTo; explicit null, duplicate fields, unknown fields, trailing JSON and invalid UTF8 are refused. Email uses the existing practical ASCII credential lookup grammar and lowercasing without trimming. Redirect validation precedes executor work. The body cap is8192 bytes even without Content-Length/chunked, with a two-second ordinary-scheduling body-read deadline. Oversized/unreadable bodies return413, body deadline408, bad JSON/email/redirect400, media/encoding415 and origin/host/fetch/query/peer admission403. Responses contain only fixed request_refused codes, never parser or provider details.

nodes.label: Uniform admitted ACK and injected executor panic/logging privacy limit
nodes.community_name: Native reset router with trusted injected admitted executor
nodes.norm_label: uniform admitted ack and injected executor panic/logging privacy limit
nodes.rationale: For every admitted executor outcome, including known/unknown account, rollback/unknown commit, postcommit delivery uncertainty or JoinError, public output is exactly200 application/json with {"status":true,"message":"If this email exists in our system, check your email for the reset link"}. Cache-Control:no-store, Referrer-Policy:no-referrer and X-Content-Type-Options:nosniff are fixed; no cookie or session is issued. Status/body/header mapping cannot expose the internal Failure stage or recipient. This is acknowledgement of the attempt, not delivery success, constant-time/constant-I/O privacy or guaranteed execution. The trusted executor must retain internal connection-reuse/commit observations before returning them. Its own logging/panic policy must exclude sensitive data; this library installs no logger/panic hook and cannot sanitize a malicious or panicking injected executor's process-wide hook output. Static router404/405 fallbacks are Axum defaults, not the admitted JSON response contract.

nodes.label: Atomic completion and fixed unknown503 without retry advice
nodes.community_name: Trusted handler HTTP recovery router without default data authority
nodes.norm_label: atomic completion and fixed unknown503 without retry advice
nodes.rationale: Completion executes password_reset::execute on the owner's admitted connection off the async loop. KDF runs outside the SQLite transaction; the current token is re-resolved under the eventual writer and password/account creation, token/sibling invalidation, session revocation, native auth-state and audit effects commit atomically. Reset possession does not grant workspace access, email verification, MFA or session authority. Only Ok after known commit maps to200 {"status":true}. NotCommitted invalid_credentials maps to source400 {"message":"Invalid token","code":"INVALID_TOKEN"}, including missing/expired/consumed/orphan recovery. Every other operational failure, OutcomeUnknown or JoinError is503 {"message":"Reset outcome could not be confirmed","code":"RESET_UNCONFIRMED"}. There is no Retry-After on these outcomes, success claim, rollback claim, automatic mutation retry or token regeneration. The trusted handler retains detailed stage/connection retirement observations internally; HTTP never exposes them.

nodes.label: Trusted handler HTTP recovery router without default data authority
nodes.community_name: Trusted handler HTTP recovery router without default data authority
nodes.norm_label: trusted handler http recovery router without default data authority

The ignored fixture helper alone opens synthetic controls from private stdin. R41/R42 and full epic acceptance remain incomplete.

nodes.label: Navigation callback strict decoded query/path and explicit HEAD405
nodes.community_name: Trusted handler HTTP recovery router without default data authority
nodes.norm_label: navigation callback strict decoded query/path and explicit head405
nodes.rationale: Mail callback is navigation, not a POST: it requires one configured canonical Host, permits missing Origin and cross-site Sec-Fetch-Site, and rejects foreign/duplicate Origin if present. It does not require a session or issue one. HEAD is explicitly405 with Allow:GET and never calls the executor or consumes callback rate/capacity; Axum's implicit HEAD behavior is deliberately overridden. The path token must be the canonical24 ASCII alphanumeric bytes; percent-encoded aliases refuse400. Exactly one literal callbackURL query key is required, including an allowed empty value; duplicates, additional keys, over8192-byte query, malformed percent escapes and invalid UTF8 refuse400. Values decode once with form plus handling. RecoveryLinks separately validates the destination against the configured origin. This rejects open redirects independently of request Origin/Host.

nodes.label: Nonconsuming callback with revalidated sensitive302 redirect
nodes.community_name: Trusted handler HTTP recovery router without default data authority
nodes.norm_label: nonconsuming callback with revalidated sensitive302 redirect
nodes.rationale: Callback invokes the existing admitted read-only reset_request::callback under a blocking permit. Existing strict unique/current token, existing-user, valid timestamp/lifetime and expiry rules decide validity; no cleanup, token consumption or reservation occurs. A valid link returns302 with a validated same-origin Location containing token; invalid/expired/consumed/orphan rows yield the trusted redirect with error=INVALID_TOKEN. Empty callback follows existing /api/auth/error?error=INVALID_TOKEN behavior. The adapter revalidates the handler's returned sensitive URL before placing it in a sensitive HeaderValue. Handler failure, wrong-origin output or panic returns fixed503 RESET_UNCONFIRMED without Location. The URL-bearing response is no-store/no-referrer/nosniff, with no cookie/session or body token JSON.

nodes.label: Retained React uncertainty flow with secret clearing and retry0
nodes.community_name: Trusted handler HTTP recovery router without default data authority
nodes.norm_label: retained react uncertainty flow with secret clearing and retry0

It offers login and a new recovery request without claiming success, invalidity or rollback, and never resubmits the old bearer. Per-call retry:0 prevents fetch-library retries. Only data.status===true with no error shows the existing success view. Known business refusals keep the existing generic refusal. The existing query-removal behavior still removes the token from navigation history. Focused UI tests cover success, known refusal and three uncertainty modes with no private provider text; app typecheck qualifies the real client signature. No browser/server deployment or whole rendered application parity is implied.

The native client uses one same-origin fetch per explicit action with no library retry loop, no redirect following and no caching; unlike BetterFetch, bare Fetch has no retry:0 option. Process-local admission is not persisted/global/proxy/header/TLS/listener/shutdown qualification. Known-commit payloads contain intentional sensitive URI/code disclosure; response/parser/serde/browser copies are not universally zeroized. HTTP no-store/no-referrer/nosniff and no private payload logging remain mandatory; trusted owner logging/panic hooks remain its responsibility.
