Source HTTP can spend quota before later rate/domain denial; source MCP lexical-date check spends neither. Shared native policy is available to eventual adapters, not claimed ported MCP/CLI. Owner create/rotate/revoke/reconcile/lost-reply lifecycle and company/dispatch/restart/restore fencing remain pending.

nodes.label: Known-commit-only context with atomic service usage mutation
nodes.community_name: Known-commit-only context with atomic service usage mutation
nodes.norm_label: known-commit-only context with atomic service usage mutation
nodes.rationale: Prepare bounded context and update only own usage/updatedAt in same writer. Authorization/projection/quota/rate/late-SQL denial rolls back all effects without destructive expired/exhausted-key cleanup. Every commit error is OutcomeUnknown, retires handle and withholds context without unchanged-usage or replay claim; precommit process death rolls back. Service GET mutates authentication metadata while business/membership/user/session/audit facts remain unchanged.

nodes.label: Locked registered service identity and current workspace access
nodes.community_name: Locked registered service identity and current workspace access
nodes.norm_label: locked registered service identity and current workspace access
nodes.rationale: Canonical BEGIN IMMEDIATE requires one unique hash across configs, correct workspace-service-principal config, enabled1, registered service/user and active member/owner access. No password/account/session/human email/MFA prerequisite. Display actual strict emailVerified and nullable twoFactorEnabled flags. Shared latest-ID memberships/catalog-order/archive/no-owner-inheritance/bounds projection excludes foreign/dangling grants. No company ledger/config/path access or later company authority; stored hashes never enter output/audit/logs.

nodes.label: Opaque service-context success and failure without credential metadata
nodes.community_name: Opaque service-context success and failure without credential metadata
nodes.norm_label: opaque service-context success and failure without credential metadata
nodes.rationale: Known commit alone returns bounded ok:true own user flags/workspace role/companies. No Set-Cookie, bearer/hash/rate internals/provider metadata/credential ID. Invalid/missing/disabled/expired/quota/rate/access401 opaque; malformed/operational/panic/unknown503 without context. Process429 separate; Retry-After reveals no key state.

nodes.label: Source inactivity-reset rate policy and native equality CAS correction
nodes.community_name: Source inactivity-reset rate policy and native equality CAS correction
nodes.norm_label: source inactivity-reset rate policy and native equality cas correction
nodes.rationale: Disabled rate updates lastRequest only. Null max/window skips rate without lastRequest/count change. Complete active policy resets count1 when lastRequest absent or elapsed>window; otherwise count<max increments and updates lastRequest. Equality does not reset. Source chooses increment at equality but CAS excludes equality and recurses; native increments under writer. Equality tested natively and excluded from frozen-clock source verifier oracle. This is inactivity-reset, not rolling/fixed-calendar600/min; default600/60000 and row overrides supported.

nodes.label: Strict service timestamps, flags and JS-safe numeric facts
nodes.community_name: Strict service timestamps, flags and JS-safe numeric facts
nodes.norm_label: strict service timestamps, flags and js-safe numeric facts
nodes.rationale: Canonical trusted millisecond dates reject future creation/update and malformed chronology. Expiry must exceed now, equality refuses; null unlimited. Optional lastRequest/refill dates cannot precede creation/future. enabled NULL/0 refuses; rateLimitEnabled NULL/1 applies and0 disables. Counters/remaining/refill/rate fields require nonnegative JS-safe integers; active complete rate fields positive. NULL/disabled policy can allow zero but never unsafe/negative/fractional facts.

Snapshot all tables permitting only own known-success usage fields. Final-quota races, contention/revocation lock, restart, late rollback, precommit death and DELETE unknown commit with no context tested. No real data/mail/deployment, full service lifecycle, physical/lifetime/drain, company writer, CLI/MCP/GPUI/distribution/cutover/full epic qualification.

Nonblank exact-untrimmed key up to4096bytes without controls and bounded workspace1024bytes; HTTP trims its one header first per source normalization. Full reversal and all R14/epic requirements remain open until their own verified acceptance.

nodes.label: Atomic audit/bank exceptions and crash/commit outcomes
nodes.community_name: Actual authenticated manual post companions in one company transaction
nodes.norm_label: atomic audit/bank exceptions and crash/commit outcomes

Resolve only open UNMATCHED_BANK_TRANSACTION exceptions attached to a positive source-bank ID, with exact source note/actor and SQLite timestamps; source helper's nonpositive-ID no-op is retained. Any companion/receipt error aborts all header/line/sequence/audit/exception effects. Process death before commit leaves none; known company commit survives control-cleanup failure, whereas commit uncertainty withholds successful posting/receipt and retires affected handle(s), with no automatic retry.

nodes.label: Canonical borrowed writer actual fact validation and active SQL constraints
nodes.community_name: Actual authenticated manual post companions in one company transaction
nodes.norm_label: canonical borrowed writer actual fact validation and active sql constraints
nodes.rationale: Storage requires main Write state, current checksummed history and exact canonical physical schema/integrity, without migration/capture/path opens. Reuse the existing compiled manual validator and source fact collector against the actual borrowed connection: accounts/roles, document register/credit-note prior posts, bank links, covering period audit lifecycle. Period locks/reopened/reported states, future horizon, balanced nonnegative one-sided lines, explicit VAT, FX and evidence checks stay active. Actual FKs/credit-note/bank-source uniqueness and append-only triggers stay active; missing optional balance-only document or already-direct bank source must not bypass SQL constraints. nodes.label: Current human authority and trusted Copenhagen posting horizon
nodes.community_name: Actual authenticated manual post companions in one company transaction
nodes.norm_label: current human authority and trusted copenhagen posting horizon
nodes.rationale: Business input is the existing strict typed ManualJournal with exact two-decimal money, six-decimal FX, canonical date/currency/identifiers and expected compiled rule version. Runtime derives actor from the CURRENT authenticated subject under the held control writer and uses fixed rentemester-rust program; caller program/actor authority is refused. Registered active company and CompanyLedgerPost permission are rechecked by the existing fence before any protected result/replay. The application reads a trusted Clock under the company transaction, converts UTC milliseconds to Europe/Copenhagen using compiled IANA data and adds runtime-configured maximum-future-days (default45), never request latestAllowedDate or host TZ. Public runtime inputs cannot override time. Chrono/Chrono-TZ are added for this required date conversion, with locked versions; APIs documented at https://docs.rs/chrono/0.4.45/chrono/struct.DateTime.html and https://docs.rs/chrono-tz/0.10.4/chrono_tz/ .

nodes.label: Fiscal numbering safe IDs and strict legacy numeric/FX precision refusal
nodes.community_name: Actual authenticated manual post companions in one company transaction
nodes.norm_label: fiscal numbering safe ids and strict legacy numeric/fx precision refusal
nodes.rationale: Read source company settings from first id row, with no-row company-1/January/end-year defaults, normalized optional DK+8digit CVR and source fiscal strategy/defaults. Allocate journal_entry companyKey:fiscalLabel sequence using the exact fiscal-prefix all-digit variable-width maximum suffix as floor, then minimum5digit suffix. IDs for header/lines/audit are checked positive JavaScript-safe MAX+1, refusing exhausted or poisoned streams rather than SQLite random fallback. Existing generated source IDs beyond this safe range and malformed metadata require explicit refusal. All new numeric storage must round-trip exact cents/micro-rate through legacy binary64 and SQLite NUMERIC; reject precision loss or nonfinite/unsafe scaled values atomically rather than silently change accounting values. Non-DKK source binary64 FX multiplication must agree with exact multiplication: ambiguous cases (for example3.00×1.005000 yielding source3.01 versus exact3.02) refuse as unsupported_legacy_number in this legacy-storage adapter. The advisory exact engine remains unchanged. Source zero-document truthiness for income/expense is preserved at this adapter boundary.

nodes.label: Actual authenticated manual post companions in one company transaction
nodes.community_name: Actual authenticated manual post companions in one company transaction
nodes.norm_label: actual authenticated manual post companions in one company transaction
nodes.rationale: Implement a real manual post through the existing authenticated human control→company fence on admitted connections. Storage writes actual canonical journal header/ordered lines, fiscal sequence, chained hash, retention, journal_post audit, bank-exception resolution and optional durable receipt in one company transaction. Canonical synthetic current-v36 ledgers qualify this use case. Original-path/lifetime/restore admission, service company quota/fence, product HTTP/CLI/MCP endpoints and outer actor-policy/backup/confirmation adapters remain required before deployment; reversal remains a separate append-only workflow. nodes.label: Same-transaction native typed idempotency without legacy fingerprint conflation
nodes.community_name: Actual authenticated manual post companions in one company transaction
nodes.norm_label: same-transaction native typed idempotency without legacy fingerprint conflation
nodes.rationale: Optional client idempotency uses journal_post plus current stable human subject and the existing durable receipt primitive inside the same transaction; authorization precedes replay. Fingerprint is the versioned native typed business request (including compiled expected version, excluding key/confirm and runtime actor/time). Typed money strings and explicit optional fields are a native protocol contract: legacy adapters must preserve their original validated fingerprint when eventually ported; this use case does not claim arbitrary prior legacy transport receipts have the same payload shape. Same native key/payload returns stored entry result without new journal companions; changed request conflicts, pruned outcome refuses and immutable key remains reserved. Business rejection returns no success receipt and retains original errors after rollback.

nodes.label: Source-compatible line/header/hash/retention storage encoding
nodes.community_name: Actual authenticated manual post companions in one company transaction
nodes.rationale: Preserve entry/line text, nullable versus empty line text and explicit ECMAScript-trimmed VAT code (no chart default). Header currency is canonical, all stored journal lines use DKK. Optional header amounts/rate are source-rounded legacy values; header status posted, reversal reference NULL, locked default1, fiscal retention deadline exact. Hash uses source declaration order, safe row identity and line ordinals, JS numeric JSON and SHA256(JSON||latest stored hash), GENESIS only when empty. Reuse the existing hash encoder and verify newly stored canonical data/hash/retention before commit. This does not invent a mandatory full prior audit/evidence-byte verification gate absent from source core.

nodes.label: Current-human append-only reversal scope without product authority
nodes.community_name: Current-human append-only reversal scope without product authority
nodes.norm_label: current-human append-only reversal scope without product authority
nodes.rationale: Implement append-only manual reversal on current canonical admitted company connections, under the existing current-human control→company writer fence and ledger.post permission. No product opener, HTTP/CLI/MCP writer, invoice repair authority, service quota admission or physical lifetime authority is introduced. Full platform goal and outer transport policy/backup/confirmation gates remain open.

nodes.label: Authorized reversal receipt and known-commit-only result
nodes.community_name: Current-human append-only reversal scope without product authority
nodes.norm_label: authorized reversal receipt and known-commit-only result
nodes.rationale: Application optionally composes JournalReverse durable receipt under stable current human principal, authorizing before replay. Every business/storage failure aborts the whole transaction. Success/receipt is released after known commit only; uncertainty withholds result and retires the affected handle. Native typed fingerprint is its own protocol, without arbitrary legacy transport fingerprint equivalence.

nodes.label: New reversal companions with immutable original and untouched exceptions
nodes.community_name: Current-human append-only reversal scope without product authority
nodes.norm_label: new reversal companions with immutable original and untouched exceptions

Insert new status reversed and reversal_of_entry_id referencing the original; never update original headers/lines or invoice/domain records. Write journal_reverse audit with current actor and source message. Do not resolve/reopen bank exceptions. Canonical reversal-shape, unique and append-only SQL guards remain enabled. Malformed or unsafe persisted numeric/identity metadata and malformed current tail hash refuse with whole rollback; newly stored hash/readback is checked, without introducing a full prior/original audit-integrity gate absent from source; legacy FX ambiguity remains an explicit adapter refusal.

nodes.label: Persisted-origin private historical/VAT context and raw metadata preservation
nodes.community_name: Current-human append-only reversal scope without product authority
nodes.norm_label: persisted-origin private historical/vat context and raw metadata preservation
nodes.rationale: Build reversal from persisted original evidence. Swap exact debit/credit, retain raw VAT including whitespace/empty versus NULL, and retain header document/bank/FX metadata. Nonempty original text becomes REVERSAL: plus raw text; NULL/empty becomes REVERSAL of original entry number. Header text uses ECMAScript-trimmed reason. Only exact persisted rentemester-import-postings with NULL document grants missing-document historical exemption and retains import program; otherwise current runtime program is used. Every reversal allows uncoded VAT control while all other active account, balance, VAT code, document/bank, period, future-date and FX validation remains enabled. These privileges are internal, never deserialized request flags; ordinary manual validation remains unchanged.

nodes.label: Actual source/process reversal acceptance scope and limits
nodes.community_name: Current-human append-only reversal scope without product authority
nodes.norm_label: actual source/process reversal acceptance scope and limits

Cover ordinary and historical/uncoded VAT positives, raw VAT/text, protected invoice negatives, period/account/bank validation, repeat reversal and source-number constraints. Real WAL/DELETE fault/death/concurrent same-original/replay/unknown-commit evidence must qualify atomicity. This contract is implementation scope, not a claim that any test or full issue already passes.

nodes.label: Strict original-ID request persisted read and protected invoice refusal precedence
nodes.community_name: Current-human append-only reversal scope without product authority
nodes.norm_label: strict original-id request persisted read and protected invoice refusal precedence
nodes.rationale: The strict request contains only original entry ID, reversal date and reason. Current actor and compiled rule version are trusted separately; business input cannot supply lines, historical/VAT policy, repair authorization, document/bank references or attribution. Original ID must be positive JavaScript-safe. Original and ordered joined lines are read inside the company writer. Preserve source refusal precedence: missing original, original itself a reversal, protected issued_invoice/credit_note document, prior reversal, no lines, then current validation. All issued invoices and credit notes are protected even without domain links; no generic repair bypass.

nodes.label: Committed charged attempt then fresh same-credential company fence
nodes.community_name: Internal admitted service company mutations without product opener
nodes.norm_label: committed charged attempt then fresh same-credential company fence
nodes.rationale: One synchronous call has two separate commits. First validate the typed envelope, workspace/key binding, trusted selected company and both connection preflights. Under control BEGIN IMMEDIATE, observe current exact live credential/registered service subject/workspace access and explicit company membership; authorize ledger.post before charging one quota/rate attempt. Commit usage and require known success. Then reacquire control BEGIN IMMEDIATE, reobserve the same exact credential ID and stable subject using the same key hash and a fresh clock, and reauthorize current company access. This second observation validates metadata but does not consume/refill again or demand remaining/rate headroom already spent by the first phase. Hold this control writer through the company commit.

nodes.label: Current service rights before receipt lookup without human-only checks
nodes.community_name: Internal admitted service company mutations without product opener
nodes.norm_label: current service rights before receipt lookup without human-only checks
nodes.rationale: A revoke/disable/rotation/expiry/membership change between phases denies company access while keeping the known charged attempt. Phase2 current authority precedes any protected receipt lookup. Workspace owner alone grants no company membership. Services need registered/live credential and active workspace/company membership, without human email/MFA/session requirements. The typed credential observation is transient trusted storage evidence, never deserialized/serialized authority or a display JSON projection.

nodes.label: Explicit recovery with original business key and no automatic retry
nodes.community_name: Internal admitted service company mutations without product opener
nodes.norm_label: explicit recovery with original business key and no automatic retry
nodes.rationale:
Recovery is explicit; this primitive performs no automatic retries:

| Usage | Business | Next safe action |
| --- | --- | --- |
| NotCommitted | NotAttempted | Correct the admission failure and deliberately retry; no committed usage or business effects are claimed. |
| OutcomeUnknown | NotAttempted | Retire control. No company callback ran. Usage has no durable per-attempt receipt, so counters under concurrency may not prove attribution; operator review or a deliberate new attempt must accept possible extra quota consumption. Do not silently retry. |
| Committed | NotAttempted / NotCommitted | Quota stays spent. Correct current authorization/business facts before any deliberate retry, retaining the original business key when the logical command is unchanged. |
| Committed | OutcomeUnknown | Retire the affected company handle. A deliberate fresh authorized attempt with the ORIGINAL idempotency key and unchanged payload can recover the committed result or execute once if absent, and may spend quota again. Without a key, inspect actual admitted journal evidence before deciding; never automatically resubmit. |
| Committed | Committed | Return only the known committed result. After a lost response, use the original business key and unchanged payload for deliberate recovery, accepting another quota charge; without a key, inspect evidence before resubmission. A committed receipt conflict is not permission to invent a fresh key. |

nodes.label: Independent usage/business commit and connection outcomes
nodes.community_name: Internal admitted service company mutations without product opener
nodes.norm_label: independent usage/business commit and connection outcomes
nodes.rationale: Outcomes report usage NotCommitted/OutcomeUnknown/Committed separately from business NotAttempted/NotCommitted/OutcomeUnknown/Committed and connection reuse flags. Only known usage commit permits company attempt; only known company commit permits successful result/receipt disclosure. Company failure never implies usage rollback. Unknown usage commit retires control and makes no company attempt. Known company success survives final control cleanup failure. Business Committed describes the company transaction, including a diagnostic-only receipt conflict; callers must inspect result.ok and must not treat stage alone as domain success. No credential secret/hash/ID is serialized, audited or logged by this orchestration.

nodes.label: Real provider/source/company process acceptance and issue limits
nodes.community_name: Internal admitted service company mutations without product opener
nodes.norm_label: real provider/source/company process acceptance and issue limits
nodes.rationale: Qualify real synthetic WAL/DELETE control and company databases, source-issued credentials/current source authorization observations and actual native post/reversal. Cover last remaining/rate slot, charged domain refusals/replays, stable subject rotation, revoked authority, between-phase revocation/expiry, real commit-busy uncertainty, killed writers and concurrent quota/same-key attempts. Compare complete company effects against actual source journals and independently verify source hashes/audits; scoped readiness and passing helpers alone do not complete R13/R14 or the epic.

nodes.label: Admitted service company mutations and report reads with explicit product HTTP/SDK/CLI/MCP scope
nodes.community_name: Internal admitted service company mutations without product opener
nodes.norm_label: admitted service company mutations and report reads with explicit product http/sdk/cli/mcp scope
nodes.rationale: Compose existing real manual post/reversal and durable receipts for service principals on admitted canonical control/company connections. No product opener or HTTP/CLI/MCP writer is enabled. Physical identity/lifetime/manifest and legacy writer admission, outer actor-policy/confirmation/backup and full platform delivery remain required.

nodes.label: Source CAS equality exclusion and explicit native authorization-charge ordering
nodes.community_name: Internal admitted service company mutations without product opener
nodes.norm_label: source cas equality exclusion and explicit native authorization-charge ordering
nodes.rationale: Preserve existing /api/me quota/refill/inactivity boundaries and strict metadata corrections, including its documented native exact-window increment correction: the installed source CAS recursively retries at equality, so frozen-clock source verification explicitly excludes that single branch and native effects are asserted directly. Source provider charges before later company authorization; this native company protocol deliberately denies known unauthorized company selection before charge, then charges later refusals. That ordering is explicit native semantics, not claimed source cross-database parity. Existing human context/post/reversal behavior must remain unchanged.

nodes.label: Stable subject receipts and separately charged attempt semantics
nodes.community_name: Internal admitted service company mutations without product opener
nodes.norm_label: stable subject receipts and separately charged attempt semantics
nodes.rationale: Real post/reversal and receipt remain atomic in the company transaction. Receipt identity is ServiceAccount plus stable service subject, never credential ID/hash/actor/path. A new valid key on the same subject can replay; a revoked old key cannot. Runtime supplies actor user:subject via service-principal; the existing reversal policy retains its verified original import marker for a historical documentless reversal. Client payload cannot control identity or attribution. Every valid new attempt, including receipt replay/conflict and later domain refusal, can consume quota again. No refund, no exactly-once logical-command quota and no cross-database atomic quota+business claim.

nodes.label: Actual SQLite handle identity and lock-preserving namespace observation
nodes.community_name: Actual open main-handle identity prerequisite without writer authority
nodes.norm_label: actual sqlite handle identity and lock-preserving namespace observation
nodes.rationale: The [SQLite identity contract](sqlite-identity/CONTRACT.md) adds a pinned bundled VFS patch and safe Rust metadata observation, consumed by WorkspaceLayout::ensure_connections. Deterministic restored-name ABA tests distinguish the actual SQLite inode from path observations. Database revalidation uses statat to preserve live POSIX locks, checked by independent child processes in WAL and DELETE. The same locked runtime passes the local lease/layout tests on Linux ARM64 container tmpfs. This is a prerequisite for persistent runtime admission; namespace ownership, the owning runtime and deployment qualification remain open.

nodes.label: Deterministic restored-name ABA and independent child-lock acceptance
nodes.community_name: Actual open main-handle identity prerequisite without writer authority
nodes.norm_label: deterministic restored-name aba and independent child-lock acceptance
nodes.rationale: Acceptance uses synthetic persistent files on the current macOS candidate filesystem and Linux ARM64 container tmpfs. The Linux run compiles the same locked source with Rust 1.94.1 and passes all 16 local lease/layout tests (3 subprocess helpers ignored outside explicit parent invocation); its image digest and source hashes are recorded separately. WAL and DELETE journal modes preserve physical identity through real transactions and reopening. A deterministic ABA swaps each database name, opens a different real SQLite file, and restores the original name before observation: the old pathname oracle passes and actual-handle comparison refuses stickily. Swapped connections, memory, added hardlinks and unlinked handles refuse. A real independent child process must remain SQLITE_BUSY before and after both ensure_current and ensure_connections while the parent holds BEGIN IMMEDIATE on either database in both journal modes; it acquires only after rollback. A further child-process test replaces the manifest with a hardlink to each live database and proves refusal still preserves its lock. These tests prevent the confirmed pre-fix accidental lock-release defect and its refused-manifest-alias variant from returning. Existing layout tests retain namespace-change and manifest checks.

nodes.label: Actual open main-handle identity prerequisite without writer authority
nodes.community_name: Actual open main-handle identity prerequisite without writer authority
nodes.norm_label: actual open main-handle identity prerequisite without writer authority
nodes.rationale: Outcome: compare the actual open SQLite main database descriptor with the control and ledger files retained by WorkspaceLayout. A pathname may be restored after SQLite opened a different inode; matching pathname observations cannot prove handle identity. This prerequisite advances persistent runtime admission. It grants no writer authority and does not complete R03/R12 or the platform epic.

nodes.label: Identity snapshot limits and pending owner/platform qualification
nodes.community_name: Actual open main-handle identity prerequisite without writer authority
nodes.norm_label: identity snapshot limits and pending owner/platform qualification
nodes.rationale: Limits: an identity snapshot does not prevent replacement after checking, qualify sidecar namespace lifetime, exclude an unenrolled same-UID legacy writer, prove fsync/power-loss durability, or admit existing user workspaces. A persistent owner still needs enforced namespace ownership, safe initialization/reopen/bootstrap, schema and logical IDs, proper close/drain/restore order, authenticated transports and OS/deployment qualification. Actual cross-UID denial, Linux host-storage and deployment qualification remain required. Container compilation/behavior is verified; no Windows/Linux deployment qualification is claimed here. Unsupported WorkspaceLayout platforms expose the same method and return UnsupportedPlatform. Tests never use real business data.

nodes.label: Pinned local SQLite dependency patch and complete provenance verification
nodes.community_name: Actual open main-handle identity prerequisite without writer authority
nodes.norm_label: pinned local sqlite dependency patch and complete provenance verification
nodes.rationale: Pin rusqlite 0.40.2 and libsqlite3-sys 0.38.2 through Cargo patches to complete vendored upstream snapshots. Retain upstream licenses, original per-file SHA256 and crates.io archive SHA256 in vendor/sqlite-provenance.json. Only four upstream files differ: rusqlite Cargo.toml, Cargo.toml.orig, src/lib.rs and bundled sqlite3/sqlite3.c. vendor/sqlite-identity.patch records the complete diff. The verifier rejects missing, extra, symlinked or changed snapshot files and mismatched patch hashes. These are application-specific dependency patches, not upstream APIs; workspace unsafe_code=forbid remains unchanged. Graphify excludes vendored upstream snapshots and indexes this contract and the runtime consumer.

nodes.label: Safe main-only integer metadata observation without pathname fallback
nodes.community_name: Actual open main-handle identity prerequisite without writer authority
nodes.norm_label: safe main-only integer metadata observation without pathname fallback
nodes.rationale: With feature rentemester_identity, safe Connection::main_file_identity fixes the schema to main, holds the connection's internal borrow through synchronous file_control, owns the initialized stack output and verifies ABI header/reserved fields. It returns only integer metadata; no pointer or descriptor escapes. Non-OK status returns its own SQLite error code without trusting a stale connection error message. Memory databases or VFSes without the patch refuse; no pathname fallback. This safe boundary assumes trusted SQLite/VFS implementations, as do existing rusqlite FFI APIs. The pinned bundled default Unix VFS is the intended consumer; arbitrary loaded native extensions/VFSes are outside the trusted runtime profile.

nodes.label: SQLite file_control reference and patch-local ABI
nodes.community_name: Actual open main-handle identity prerequisite without writer authority
nodes.norm_label: sqlite file_control reference and patch-local abi
nodes.rationale: References: SQLite's [file_control contract](https://www.sqlite.org/c3ref/file_control.html) routes a named database to its VFS xFileControl; [standard opcodes](https://www.sqlite.org/c3ref/c_fcntl_begin_atomic_write.html) document the existing file-pointer and moved-name observations. The new opcode is local to the pinned patch and its exact ABI above.

nodes.label: Lock-preserving database statat and required descriptor lifetime order
nodes.community_name: Actual open main-handle identity prerequisite without writer authority
nodes.norm_label: lock-preserving database statat and required descriptor lifetime order
nodes.rationale: Database-name revalidation must not open or close ordinary file descriptors for either SQLite inode. Closing such a descriptor can cancel another SQLite connection's POSIX locks held by the same process. ensure_current now uses descriptor-relative no-follow statat from retained parent directories for all regular names, including the manifest; retained-file metadata uses fstat. Manifest bytes are reread with read_at on the retained file, without cloning/opening/closing it. A manifest replaced with a hardlink to a live database must refuse without releasing that database lock. Only directory components are reopened with DIRECTORY/NOFOLLOW. bind must occur before opening SQLite connections, and the eventual owning runtime must close every SQLite handle before dropping the retained layout descriptors. This increment does not introduce that owning runtime or permit arbitrary lifetime order to serve writes.

nodes.label: Sticky retained control/ledger actual-handle comparison
nodes.community_name: Actual open main-handle identity prerequisite without writer authority
nodes.rationale: WorkspaceLayout::ensure_connections first and last checks the retained layout and compares both actual main handles against the exact retained control/ledger device and inode. A current single link is required. Any mismatch or observation error permanently invalidates the layout; restoring names or supplying different handles cannot revive it. Read-only handles may match this physical observation: connection write mode, canonical schema/logical identity, actor authorization and writer admission remain separate required checks.

nodes.label: Unix VFS actual-descriptor identity opcode and initialized ABI
nodes.community_name: Actual open main-handle identity prerequisite without writer authority
nodes.norm_label: unix vfs actual-descriptor identity opcode and initialized abi
nodes.rationale: The Unix VFS implements application opcode 0x524d0101 in unixFileControl. The caller supplies eight aligned initialized 64-bit words with magic 0x524d4944454e5431 and ABI version 1. After validating the header the VFS clears the full buffer, fstats its actual unixFile.h descriptor and requires a regular file. It returns magic/version/device/inode/mode/link-count and two zero reserved words. Invalid ABI is SQLITE_MISUSE, missing descriptor/nonregular file is SQLITE_NOTFOUND and fstat failure is SQLITE_IOERR_FSTAT. It does not stat a pathname, expose descriptors, alter SQLite locks, pager, journals or namespace operations. Other VFSes and the SQLCipher amalgamation do not implement the opcode.

nodes.label: Descriptor-bound layout with retained cooperative lease
nodes.community_name: Actual open main-handle identity prerequisite without writer authority
nodes.norm_label: descriptor-bound layout with retained cooperative lease
nodes.rationale: Outcome: consume the existing cooperative WorkspaceLease and bind one existing registered company's physical layout through no-follow descriptor-relative opens. Retain the root lease, manifest, control directory/file, selected company directory/data directory/file. All six descendant identities remain pinned until Drop. Source paths are workspace.json, .rentemester/workspace-control.sqlite and <slug>/data/ledger.sqlite. Never create, migrate, recover, open SQLite connections or write source files. No product writer is enabled.

nodes.label: Physical layout acceptance and ownership/death evidence
nodes.community_name: Actual open main-handle identity prerequisite without writer authority
nodes.norm_label: physical layout acceptance and ownership/death evidence
nodes.rationale: Acceptance: synthetic canonical layouts bind without changing names/bytes; wrong keys/slugs/manifest types/duplicates/archives and every unsafe path level refuse; revalidation detects root/manifest/control/company/data/ledger replacement, in-place manifest changes and hardlink introduction, stays invalid after restoration and retains ownership until Drop. Ordinary ledger bytes/size changes do not invalidate physical binding. Real processes prove a held layout excludes a second root lease and process death releases it. Existing lease checks plus native format/Clippy/runtime tests pass; independent review inspects the descriptor and manifest boundaries. This is physical layout observation, not database-handle qualification or completed writer admission.

nodes.label: Same-device distinct no-follow single-link component bindings
nodes.community_name: Actual open main-handle identity prerequisite without writer authority
nodes.norm_label: same-device distinct no-follow single-link component bindings
nodes.rationale: All path segments below the already held root use openat with NOFOLLOW/CLOEXEC/NONBLOCK, and DIRECTORY for directories. Final files must be regular single-link files; reject symlinks, hardlinks, FIFOs, devices, missing paths and control/ledger aliasing. Require every component on the root device and all component identities distinct, including the root; descendant mounts/aliases on other devices are unsupported. Keep file descriptors private, non-Clone and unexposed. Binding errors have fixed codes and never include source bytes or credentials. Require an unchanged root before and after binding; compare the manifest descriptor identity and SHA256 bytes again before returning. Existing candidate-filesystem limitations of WorkspaceLease remain.

nodes.label: Sticky invalidation on namespace or manifest generation changes
nodes.community_name: Actual open main-handle identity prerequisite without writer authority
nodes.norm_label: sticky invalidation on namespace or manifest generation changes
nodes.rationale: ensure_current observes exact descriptor-relative paths, using no-follow statat for all regular names and read_at on the retained manifest to avoid opening/closing even a substituted manifest alias to a live SQLite inode and releasing process POSIX locks, and compares held and current device/inode identities and required type/link count, and checks exact manifest identity/content. Root loss or any layout change invalidates the object permanently; restoration cannot revive it. Retain the root lock and old descriptors until Drop. Changes in ledger/control contents or file size are permitted: those are transaction-owned data, not namespace changes. Namespace observation is not an atomic fence against a local OS actor replacing/restoring files between observations. Legitimate future namespace/manifest operations must obey the same lifetime ownership protocol; current unpatched legacy entrypoints still do not.

nodes.label: Strict typed bounded v1 manifest and runtime workspace association
nodes.community_name: Actual open main-handle identity prerequisite without writer authority
nodes.norm_label: strict typed bounded v1 manifest and runtime workspace association
nodes.rationale: Configuration supplies an explicit nonblank workspace key and exact safe company slug. The key is a runtime association, not a newly invented persistent logical identity: the current v1 manifest contains no stable workspace UUID. Parse a bounded1MiB UTF8 JSON manifest with exact version1, typed fields, unique safe company slugs and exact Boolean archived. Reject missing/malformed/oversize/duplicate/unknown fields and invalid entries rather than legacy String/Boolean coercions. Names and createdAt are bounded nonblank non-control metadata; createdAt is not interpreted as an authority timestamp. Require exact registration and a nonarchived selected company. Archived entries remain legal for other companies. No unlisted-company adoption or default manifest.

nodes.label: Private descriptors, actual handle observation and pending lifetime admission
nodes.community_name: Actual open main-handle identity prerequisite without writer authority
nodes.norm_label: private descriptors, actual handle observation and pending lifetime admission
nodes.rationale: Expose bound workspace key, selected slug, ensure_current and the later ensure_connections observation. Keep descriptors private and never turn recorded identities into write authority. The SQLite-identity increment adds actual open-handle comparison through a pinned VFS dependency patch; see ../sqlite-identity/CONTRACT.md. Path equality or matching before/after stat alone remains insufficient. Bind before SQLite opens; close all SQLite handles before dropping this layout. The persistent owning runtime and namespace lifetime admission remain required before trusted writers. Stable logical identity/clone lineage, runtime generation, all legacy mutation enrollment, IPC, storage/platform qualification, actual authenticated posting and full R03/R12/R13 acceptance remain pending.

nodes.label: Private retry-only close failure and unresolved process-exit quarantine
nodes.community_name: Private persistent Linux broker owner without product deployment authority
nodes.norm_label: private retry-only close failure and unresolved process-exit quarantine
nodes.rationale: A `CloseFailure` privately owns a boxed retired owner. Its sole operation is `retry`; it does not expose the owner or connections. Dropping an owner or close failure retries explicit closure. If any close still fails, it forgets the entire unresolved resource set, intentionally quarantining the handles, pins and lease until process exit. It never finalizes unowned statements or relies on ordinary `Connection::Drop`, which discards sqlite3_close failure. Process termination lets the OS release those resources. Quarantine is a last-resort safety behavior, not a recovery or availability guarantee.

nodes.label: Consuming confirmed per-slot close before guard release
nodes.community_name: Private persistent Linux broker owner without product deployment authority
nodes.norm_label: consuming confirmed per-slot close before guard release
nodes.rationale: `try_close(self)` retires the owner and calls consuming `Connection::close` on both slots. Every successful close removes that slot; an `Err((connection, error))` restores the exact still-open connection. The guard, all pinned descriptors and workspace lease remain until **every** connection is confirmed closed. Other successfully closed slots need not remain open.

nodes.label: Four fixed application dispatch methods using bound registered selection
nodes.community_name: Private persistent Linux broker owner without product deployment authority
nodes.norm_label: four fixed application dispatch methods using bound registered selection
nodes.rationale: Four public methods directly invoke the frozen application use cases: `post_human`, `reverse_human`, `post_service`, `reverse_service`. The selected workspace/slug come from the owned layout binding and revalidated manifest; callers cannot claim a different registration/archive status. The application retains its actual authorization, session/key, role, idempotency and transaction policy. Trusted adapters still own credential verification and transport-specific gates; these methods are not HTTP endpoints.

nodes.label: Namespace guard before private NOFOLLOW existing connection open
nodes.community_name: Private persistent Linux broker owner without product deployment authority
nodes.norm_label: namespace guard before private nofollow existing connection open
nodes.rationale: `Owner::open_protected(root, broker_uid, workspace, slug)` first acquires the dedicated-UID `NamespaceGuard`, including the workspace lease and pinned layout. Only then does it open the two named files with READ_WRITE and NOFOLLOW, without CREATE or URI flags. It configures foreign keys and FULL synchronous mode and verifies actual handles against the retained layout. It does not choose new journal modes or expose a connection supplied by a caller.

nodes.label: No callback or connection extraction API to preserve lifetime ownership
nodes.community_name: Private persistent Linux broker owner without product deployment authority
nodes.norm_label: no callback or connection extraction api to preserve lifetime ownership
nodes.rationale: There is no public generic callback, mutable connection reference, raw handle, connection-bearing failure, conversion, Deref or AsMut. A generic callback could move out a connection with safe `mem::replace`; even a callback returning unit could capture it. Such an API would invalidate lifetime ownership and is deliberately absent.

nodes.label: Offline provisioning lineage and implicit SQLite recovery trust limits
nodes.community_name: Private persistent Linux broker owner without product deployment authority
nodes.norm_label: offline provisioning lineage and implicit sqlite recovery trust limits
nodes.rationale: The launcher's strict Linux profile, root/operator and all enrolled broker-UID code remain trusted. Separate client/legacy UIDs cannot obtain new file access. Provisioning must be offline and protect files from creation; the guard cannot revoke prior, inherited or passed descriptors. Current metadata does not establish absence of earlier clients. This constructor alone does not prove native schema, logical lineage, prior-writer drain, authentication bootstrap, or permission to adopt existing data. SQLite may perform ordinary hot-journal/WAL recovery when opening/configuring existing files; this is a possible persistent effect even without an explicit repair command.

nodes.label: Partial construction retains shared resource close discipline
nodes.community_name: Private persistent Linux broker owner without product deployment authority
nodes.norm_label: partial construction retains shared resource close discipline
nodes.rationale: Every partially constructed owner already holds its connections and namespace in one private resource set. A later open, configuration or identity error drops that set through the same explicit-close mechanism as shutdown. No CREATE, chmod, chown, unlink, namespace repair or migration is performed by this crate.

nodes.norm_label: pending canonical domain success and transport/platform delivery acceptance

nodes.community_name: Private persistent Linux broker owner without product deployment authority
nodes.norm_label: persistent close-busy/retry/partial-construction and external api acceptance
nodes.rationale: The qualification covers normal commit/confirmed close/persistent reopen in WAL and DELETE, actual close BUSY on each database, retry, Drop quarantine, process-exit release, partial-constructor clean/error/panic paths, sticky namespace invalidation/restoration and dispatch-admission panic. Independent compile-fail consumers check the absence of connection extraction APIs.

nodes.label: Private persistent Linux broker owner without product deployment authority
nodes.community_name: Private persistent Linux broker owner without product deployment authority
nodes.norm_label: private persistent linux broker owner without product deployment authority
nodes.rationale: The `rentemester-host` crate composes the existing namespace guard with privately owned control and company SQLite connections. This increment is the physical owning runtime for an offline-provisioned Linux broker, not a production writer, schema adoption, fresh initializer, bootstrap, transport, or deployment qualification. The existing general product and all 55 epic issues remain the goal; local macOS and remote desktop modes remain required.

nodes.label: Retire before dispatch and preserve exact application outcome
nodes.community_name: Private persistent Linux broker owner without product deployment authority
nodes.norm_label: retire before dispatch and preserve exact application outcome
nodes.rationale: Admission marks the owner retired *before* revalidation and dispatch. An error or unwinding panic cannot silently restore it. Only an application result whose connection reuse flags allow it, followed by successful physical revalidation, makes the owner reusable. `Attempt` preserves the exact original application result and separately reports retirement. A committed/unknown outcome must not turn into a fresh retry merely because the owner retires afterward. No operation is admitted on a retired owner.

nodes.label: Scoped structural readiness and real isolated UID fixture scope
nodes.community_name: Private persistent Linux broker owner without product deployment authority
nodes.norm_label: scoped structural readiness and real isolated uid fixture scope
nodes.rationale: `readiness.json` is scoped structural GDD readiness, not behavioral proof. The model was written during implementation, not a claim of pre-implementation validation. Native tests use real persistent files and child-process lock contenders. Test-only fault hooks are excluded from the production build.

nodes.label: Trusted owner encapsulation without live regular-file reopening or sandbox claim
nodes.community_name: Private persistent Linux broker owner without product deployment authority
nodes.norm_label: trusted owner encapsulation without live regular-file reopening or sandbox claim
nodes.rationale: The implementation contains no ordinary regular-file reopening/copy/hash operations while owned handles are live. The application and code compiled in the owner module remain trusted. This is API encapsulation, not a sandbox for malicious same-UID code.

nodes.label: Both-empty connection preflight and caller fresh-file provenance
nodes.community_name: Exclusive fresh native workspace without existing-data or bootstrap authority
nodes.norm_label: both-empty connection preflight and caller fresh-file provenance
nodes.rationale: `fresh::initialize_empty_pair` operates solely on caller-owned connections. The caller must prove fresh-file provenance and exclusive physical ownership. Both databases preflight before persistent SQL: writable, autocommit, no main or temp objects, no attached databases, zero user_version/application_id and query_only off. Company metadata must be valid. Empty schema alone is not proof that an older file was never used; the host supplies the proof by exclusive new creation.

nodes.norm_label: checksum-bound complete canonical control30/company36 schema builders

nodes.norm_label: creation descriptors close before sqlite and original lease transfers continuously

nodes.label: Exclusive fresh native workspace without existing-data or bootstrap authority
nodes.community_name: Exclusive fresh native workspace without existing-data or bootstrap authority
nodes.norm_label: exclusive fresh native workspace without existing-data or bootstrap authority

nodes.label: Exclusive protected namespace and fsync before SQLite
nodes.community_name: Exclusive fresh native workspace without existing-data or bootstrap authority
nodes.norm_label: exclusive protected namespace and fsync before sqlite
nodes.rationale: `NamespaceGuard::create_fresh` uses mkdirat with exclusive creation semantics relative to the checked parent and 0700 mode. It validates the resulting ancestry and acquires the root lease before creating internal directories and regular files. Files use CREATE|EXCL|NOFOLLOW,0600 and explicit fsync; directories and parent are synced. No actual existing workspace is opened or modified by this operation. Parent and new root identities are compared, and the held lease's identity must match the checked directory.

nodes.label: Every existing root refused and failed private partial tree retained
nodes.community_name: Exclusive fresh native workspace without existing-data or bootstrap authority
nodes.norm_label: every existing root refused and failed private partial tree retained
nodes.rationale: Existing directories, regular files and symlinks all return `workspace_exists`. Even an empty existing directory is not reused. There is no CREATE IF NOT EXISTS, adoption, repair, chmod/chown, recursive deletion or best-effort resume of a failed creation. Invalid input or unsafe parent/process refuses before the new directory is created. A supported process can still fail after mkdir, for example on an unsupported filesystem or I/O error; the new private partial tree is retained for inspection and a later create refuses it.

nodes.label: Independent database commits and truthful partial initialization failure
nodes.community_name: Exclusive fresh native workspace without existing-data or bootstrap authority
nodes.norm_label: independent database commits and truthful partial initialization failure
nodes.rationale: The two database commits are independent, not atomic together. If company initialization fails after control commits, control can be complete while company remains empty. No initialized report/owner is returned; the whole owning constructor closes safely or quarantines unresolved handles, and the private partial tree remains. No retry/adoption capability is granted. Tests exercise real company write contention and check that the completed control and untouched company are observable accurately.

It reruns the existing 50 physical-owner checks. Only synthetic files are created in task-owned Docker volumes; no real workspace is mounted.

nodes.label: Retired guarded constructor and close/quarantine resource discipline
nodes.community_name: Exclusive fresh native workspace without existing-data or bootstrap authority
nodes.norm_label: retired guarded constructor and close/quarantine resource discipline

nodes.label: Committed, not_committed and unknown outcomes with cleanup/crash semantics
nodes.norm_label: committed, not_committed and unknown outcomes with cleanup/crash semantics
nodes.rationale: Success commits the company transaction before releasing the control lock by explicit rollback. SQLite control writers such as disable, revoke, exact session deletion and MFA invalidation can commit either before admission (then deny) or after the company commit, never between the protected observation and commit. Control is never deliberately written. Cleanup failure after a known company commit returns the committed value with control_reusable=false; it cannot be represented as a pre-commit failure. A company commit error or lost transaction reports outcome_unknown and requires retiring affected connections/recovery using the future durable receipt. Before any company commit attempt, callback/SQL/authorization failures explicitly roll back and report not_committed with per-connection reuse status; rollback failures require retirement. Panics/process death rely on SQLite rollback/lock release; a crash after ledger commit preserves the commit. Already allowed results and prior receipts never bypass new authorization.

nodes.label: Internal synchronous control-to-company fence contract
nodes.rationale: This R04/R13 storage/application increment implements an internal synchronous transaction path over two caller-owned admitted SQLite connections. It does not open source paths or enable a product mutation endpoint. The full epic and identity-provider decision remain open.

nodes.label: Barrier/crash transaction mechanics acceptance without product writer completion
nodes.norm_label: barrier/crash transaction mechanics acceptance without product writer completion
nodes.rationale: Acceptance: actual canonical synthetic control stores plus isolated transaction-effect ledgers; current-row denial and full-width/latest-ID cases; exact permission and scope refusal; active/deferred transaction, attach/temp, disabled FK/durability and read-only admission refusal; successful company commit with no control data effects; business/SQL failure after sequence and companion writes rolls both back; callback transaction escape reports unknown. Barrier-driven separate processes prove revoke-first denial, revoke blocked while the fence is held, pre-commit killed/reaped child rollback and post-commit killed/reaped child preservation. Repeat over WAL and rollback journals where supported, preserving source/protected fixtures and all previous access-policy checks. Such effect ledgers prove transaction mechanics, not complete accounting schema/domain admission or hardware power-loss qualification. Final format, Clippy, targeted native/process suites and independent review must pass; GDD scoped readiness precedes implementation. No real company data may be used.

nodes.label: Qualified WAL/DELETE connections and locked actual control rows
nodes.norm_label: qualified wal/delete connections and locked actual control rows
nodes.rationale: Both connections must be initially autocommit, have no attached or temporary objects, foreign_keys ON, synchronous FULL/EXTRA and journal_mode WAL or DELETE. OFF, MEMORY and all other unqualified journal modes refuse before callback; in-memory execute connections are not admitted. The runtime must bind distinct, stable physical/logical databases and enforce one global control-before-company lock order for all entrypoints. Existing TypeScript writes are not enrolled by this increment; originals remain forbidden until lifetime admission/cutover. The API rejects public/workspace permissions before any callback. It establishes control BEGIN IMMEDIATE, admits the complete current checksummed control schema/history and integrity/FKs, reads exact current user/session membership and latest workspace/company access by signed SQLite event ID (never timestamp), and evaluates the shared Rust policy. Missing/deleted or wrong-user session, missing/unready user, disabled workspace, revoked membership, archive or cross-scope observations deny without executing business work. Current control rows override supplied company membership; no client role is accepted.

nodes.label: Trusted provider observation and manifest lifetime prerequisites
nodes.norm_label: trusted provider observation and manifest lifetime prerequisites
nodes.rationale: The caller supplies a trusted provider-authenticated human session observation (workspace key, exact subject/session IDs, provider authentication readiness), a registered company selection bound to its workspace and slug, and the operation's statically chosen company permission. None of these observations implements Deserialize. A claimed actor, supplied role, held process lease or session-row ID alone is not authentication. The provider must already have verified credentials, session expiry and any required MFA/session assurance. Services/local identities require their own later adapters. Company registration/archive/path identity must remain fenced by the caller's lifetime/manifest admission; SQLite alone does not protect workspace.json.

nodes.label: Trusted synchronous company callback transaction boundary
nodes.norm_label: trusted synchronous company callback transaction boundary
nodes.rationale: Only after authorization does it establish company BEGIN IMMEDIATE. Trusted synchronous callback work uses that transaction, with no await, network, external effects, transaction-control SQL, connection close, other connections or control writes. Journal/evidence/rule/confirmation/backup checks and atomic receipts belong to the eventual callback/use case; this increment is not posting or idempotency completion. Callbacks are trusted Rust code, not sandboxed SQL. A detected manual callback commit/lost transaction yields an uncertain-outcome failure, never an ordinary refusal.

nodes.label: Bounded local iXBRL taxonomy
nodes.rationale: The declared regnskabsklasse B subset limits output to listed facts and stable local namespace; filing remains owner/advisor responsibility.

nodes.label: Fixed-asset depreciation
nodes.rationale: Deterministic balanced period postings remain linked to purchase evidence; user/advisor chooses plan and tax treatment.

nodes.label: Period-bounded authority export
nodes.rationale: Structured journal and readable vouchers are assembled for a requested period with manifest and deadline.

nodes.label: Weekly signed backup and restore
nodes.rationale: Full ledger and document backups require hashes, signing-key history, destination attestation and verified restoration.

nodes.label: Vendor master-data resolution
nodes.rationale: Reused sender data must resolve to an append-only vendor record and be materialized at ingest.

nodes.label: GDPR subject access export
nodes.rationale: Article 15 flow gives a structured export while preserving prior redactions.

nodes.label: Danish Class B annual report
nodes.rationale: Prepared only for a fully locked, balanced year with registered CVR and complete company data.

nodes.label: Append-only journal and reversal
nodes.rationale: Posted entries remain immutable; one linked mirrored reversal provides correction traceability.

nodes.label: Fixed-asset depreciation must post deterministic, balanced period entries linked to the purchase
nodes.norm_label: fixed-asset depreciation must post deterministic, balanced period entries linked to the purchase
nodes.rationale: Rentemester assists the bookkeeping workflow by capitalising an asset and posting deterministic, balanced depreciation entries that stay linked to the original purchase documentation; the user/advisor remains responsible for choosing the depreciation plan and tax treatment.

nodes.label: Posted journal entries are append-only
nodes.rationale: Once posted, entries are locked. Corrections must be new reversing/correcting entries with audit trail.

nodes.label: Bookkeeping data and vouchers must be exportable by period in a structured machine-readable package
nodes.norm_label: bookkeeping data and vouchers must be exportable by period in a structured machine-readable package
nodes.rationale: Rentemester must be able to assemble bookkeeping transactions and related vouchers for a requested period in a structured machine-readable format, alongside readable document files and a traceable deadline for a four-week authority handover flow.

nodes.label: The system must support weekly full backups of booked transactions and supporting documents
nodes.norm_label: the system must support weekly full backups of booked transactions and supporting documents
nodes.rationale: Rentemester must be able to create a full backup of bookkeeping data and supporting documents and deterministically report when the weekly backup duty has become due because new activity happened after the last backup.

nodes.label: Double-entry postings must balance
nodes.rationale: Ledger postings must be balanced. Rentemester rejects unbalanced journal entries before they can be posted.

nodes.label: Imported bank transactions must preserve transaction date, amount, text, and traceable source batch
nodes.norm_label: imported bank transactions must preserve transaction date, amount, text, and traceable source batch
nodes.rationale: Rentemester must import bank transactions with enough metadata to support prompt registration, control trail, and deterministic deduplication.

nodes.label: Journal postings must stay out of closed periods and must not be future-dated
nodes.norm_label: journal postings must stay out of closed periods and must not be future-dated
nodes.rationale: Rentemester must block postings whose transaction date falls inside a closed or reported accounting period, and must also reject future-dated journal entries so historical VAT and bookkeeping periods stay stable.

nodes.label: Bank reconciliation must show matched and unmatched imported transactions for a period
nodes.norm_label: bank reconciliation must show matched and unmatched imported transactions for a period
nodes.rationale: Rentemester must be able to deterministically reconcile imported bank transactions against posted journal entries so reporting has an updated control basis.

nodes.label: Supporting material must carry a retention deadline from the end of the fiscal year plus five years
nodes.norm_label: supporting material must carry a retention deadline from the end of the fiscal year plus five years
nodes.rationale: Rentemester must track a deterministic retention deadline for bookkeeping material based on the end of the fiscal year the material relates to, and surface overdue material without deleting it automatically.

nodes.label: Corrections must create a single traceable reversal entry
nodes.norm_label: corrections must create a single traceable reversal entry
nodes.rationale: Rentemester must correct a posted entry by appending one linked reversal entry that mirrors the original lines with opposite signs and leaves the original intact.

nodes.label: Double-entry balance invariant
nodes.rationale: Debit and credit sums must match before posting.

nodes.label: Digital voucher minimum fields
nodes.rationale: Stored purchase and sales documents need statutory metadata, with explicit exceptions for cash receipts and foreign physical-only documents.

nodes.label: Original supporting documents must be preserved without silent overwrite or mutation
nodes.norm_label: original supporting documents must be preserved without silent overwrite or mutation
nodes.rationale: Stored supporting documents must be kept on a secure, traceable basis so the original content is preserved and duplicates are not silently mutated or overwritten.

nodes.label: Purchase and sale supporting documents stored digitally must include the statutory minimum fields
nodes.norm_label: purchase and sale supporting documents stored digitally must include the statutory minimum fields
nodes.rationale: Rentemester must reject digitally stored purchase/sale supporting documents that lack the statutory minimum metadata unless an explicit legal exception applies.

nodes.norm_label: vendor master data reused on supporting documents must resolve deterministically before ingest

nodes.label: Erasure requests must respect the bookkeeping retention deadline before redacting personal data in regnskabsmateriale
nodes.norm_label: erasure requests must respect the bookkeeping retention deadline before redacting personal data in regnskabsmateriale
nodes.rationale: GDPR article 17, stk. 3, lit. b og e tillader at retten til sletning fraviges når behandlingen er nødvendig for at overholde en retlig forpligtelse eller udføres i offentlighedens interesse. Bogføringspligten (LOV 700/2022 § 12 — 5 års opbevaring fra regnskabsårets udgang) er sådan en retlig forpligtelse. Rentemester nægter derfor sletning af regnskabsmateriale inden for retention-vinduet, gemmer afgørelsen som append-only tombstone i gdpr_erasures, og lader retention-deadlinen (DK-BOOKKEEPING-RETENTION-001) styre hvornår en senere sletning bliver lovlig. Flowet ligger i src/core/gdpr.ts og er rule_id GDPR-RETENTION-BOUNDED-ERASURE i audit-loggen.

nodes.label: A data subject must be able to obtain a structured copy of their personal data held by the bookkeeping system
nodes.norm_label: a data subject must be able to obtain a structured copy of their personal data held by the bookkeeping system
nodes.rationale: Rentemester implements GDPR article 15 (right of access) by assembling a deterministic export of all personal-data fields tied to a named subject (cvr or natural-person name), with previously-redacted fields kept redacted so an erasure request stays effective in subsequent exports. The flow lives in src/core/gdpr.ts and is rule_id GDPR-SUBJECT-EXPORT in the audit log.

nodes.label: Retention-bounded erasure
nodes.rationale: Article 17 erasure is refused within bookkeeping retention; decisions become append-only tombstones and later action follows retention deadlines.

nodes.label: Exact23 permissions and two/four role matrix
nodes.community_name: Shared Rust access policy decision contract
nodes.norm_label: exact23 permissions and two/four role matrix
nodes.rationale: `Permission`, `WorkspaceRole` and `CompanyRole` use the exact existing 23 permission strings and two/four role strings. Unknown vocabulary refuses deserialization. `role_allows` is only a presentation/policy-table query. Workspace ownership grants no implicit company access. Company owner grants every explicitly enumerated company permission, never future unknown permissions. Bookkeeper/reviewer/reader retain the exact current matrix, including knowledge/ownership exceptions.

nodes.label: Independent actual legacy policy acceptance and explicit differences
nodes.community_name: Shared Rust access policy decision contract
nodes.norm_label: independent actual legacy policy acceptance and explicit differences
nodes.rationale: Acceptance: independent fixed Python policy matrix (all roles/permissions/security states plus explicit binding counterexamples), native Rust output versus those fixed expectations, actual unchanged TypeScript role policy and source-backed `authorizeWorkspaceRoute` on synthetic current control stores for corresponding cases, strict unknown vocabulary rejection, immutable inputs and repeated calls. Retain explicit differences: Rust requires a verified credential/session observation while legacy core assumes an upstream authenticated caller and accepts any registered service-account row; do not pass caller-controlled facts to product APIs. Domain/application dependency guards must reject I/O/storage/transport dependencies. Scoped GDD readiness precedes implementation; format, Clippy, native tests, corpus parity and existing regression checks must pass. Only synthetic files may be written.

nodes.label: Non-disclosing decisions and future revocation obligations
nodes.community_name: Shared Rust access policy decision contract
nodes.norm_label: non-disclosing decisions and future revocation obligations
nodes.rationale: No denial detail distinguishes missing companies, identities, security readiness, membership or insufficient role. Repeated evaluation of immutable observations is deterministic and has no effects. A prior allowed result never authorizes later work: integration MUST load/reauthorize under the future control/ledger revocation fence and reauthorize before returning protected idempotency receipts. This increment does not establish that fence, session verification, credential lifecycle, last-owner mutation guards, source adapters, stable persisted IDs, R04 identity-provider selection, or full R13 acceptance.

nodes.label: Shared Rust access policy decision contract
nodes.community_name: Shared Rust access policy decision contract
nodes.norm_label: shared rust access policy decision contract
nodes.rationale: This R13 increment creates `rentemester-application::access` for the common workspace/company route decision. It consumes already authenticated, current control facts supplied by an in-process trusted adapter and returns only `Decision { allowed }`. It performs no I/O, has no ambient actor fallback, issues no authorization capability and is not exposed through a product transport. The complete epic remains the goal.

nodes.label: Trusted non-Deserialize authenticated observations
nodes.community_name: Shared Rust access policy decision contract
nodes.rationale: `authorize` receives an explicit workspace key and optional company slug, an optional identity observation, optional workspace access and optional company observation. These facts do NOT implement `Deserialize`. They are not authentication claims from a JSON request. An identity must have nonempty exact workspace/subject keys, match the requested workspace and be authenticated. Humans require both verified email and enabled MFA; service identities require a registered service account AND verified live credential. A human may not use the service-account bypass. Local actor policy/authentication requires a separate adapter; an actor string or held workspace lease is insufficient.

nodes.label: Public precedence and exact workspace/subject/company isolation
nodes.community_name: Shared Rust access policy decision contract
nodes.norm_label: public precedence and exact workspace/subject/company isolation
nodes.rationale: Public read and invitation claim allow anonymous access as in the current policy; claiming still requires its separate invitation validation. A generic route allow is not approval for every operation: service credential administration still requires a hosted human session even when a service role allows `workspace.manage`. Every private permission requires active workspace access matching both exact workspace and subject. Workspace permissions use only the workspace role and ignore company data. Company permissions additionally require an exact ASCII slug (`[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]*`), registered nonarchived company in the requested workspace and active membership matching workspace, subject and company. Cross-workspace, cross-subject and cross-company observations refuse. No trimming, case folding, environment lookup, path inference or ID creation occurs; an adapter must resolve source values before calling.
