nodes.label: Danish VAT treatment and reporting
nodes.rationale: Versioned VAT codes and rules distinguish domestic, EU/non-EU reverse charge, representation, bad-debt relief, OSS and registration state; omitted EU-goods VAT remains an explicit out-of-scope gap.

nodes.label: Established bad-debt losses on standard-rated sales must reduce output VAT from the deductible 80 percent loss basis
nodes.norm_label: established bad-debt losses on standard-rated sales must reduce output vat from the deductible 80 percent loss basis
nodes.rationale: When an issued Danish standard-rated invoice becomes an established bad debt, Rentemester must write off the gross receivable, expense the deductible loss basis, and reduce output VAT deterministically for the same loss amount.

nodes.label: Cross-border B2B sales without Danish VAT must be listed per customer VAT number for the EU sales list
nodes.norm_label: cross-border b2b sales without danish vat must be listed per customer vat number for the eu sales list
nodes.rationale: Rentemester must deterministically derive the EU sales list (EU-salg uden moms) by grouping cross-border B2B sales without Danish VAT per customer VAT number, so the business can file the separate recapitulative statement alongside the momsangivelse.

nodes.label: A filing-ready momsangivelse may only be produced for a closed VAT period and must map data into the standard SKAT rubrikker
nodes.norm_label: a filing-ready momsangivelse may only be produced for a closed vat period and must map data into the standard skat rubrikker
nodes.rationale: A momsangivelse must only be produced for a closed or reported vat_quarter period and must deterministically map the VAT settlement data into the standard SKAT rubrikker so the business can file via TastSelv with traceable numbers.

nodes.label: Non-registered companies absorb input VAT into the expense basis
nodes.norm_label: non-registered companies absorb input vat into the expense basis

nodes.label: Digital-service sales to EU consumers under the OSS scheme must be kept out of the standard momsangivelse
nodes.norm_label: digital-service sales to eu consumers under the oss scheme must be kept out of the standard momsangivelse

nodes.label: VAT registration is a first-class company state
nodes.norm_label: vat registration is a first-class company state

nodes.label: VAT settlement basis must show output VAT, input VAT, and net payable for a period
nodes.norm_label: vat settlement basis must show output vat, input vat, and net payable for a period
nodes.rationale: Rentemester must deterministically derive the VAT settlement basis for a period from traceable journal data so the business can reconcile and file VAT correctly.

nodes.label: Representation purchases with limited VAT deduction must only book 25 percent of the VAT as deductible input tax
nodes.norm_label: representation purchases with limited vat deduction must only book 25 percent of the vat as deductible input tax
nodes.rationale: Rentemester must deterministically split representation purchases so only 25 percent of the full VAT is booked as deductible input VAT, while the remaining VAT is kept in the expense basis.

nodes.label: EU service reverse-charge purchases must book both output and deductible input VAT in the period
nodes.norm_label: eu service reverse-charge purchases must book both output and deductible input vat in the period
nodes.rationale: Rentemester must deterministically book reverse-charge VAT on EU service purchases so VAT reporting includes both the payment liability and the deductible input tax when applicable.

nodes.label: Native precommit verification message postcommit handoff and truthful destination
nodes.community_name: Verification composition without public HTTP or legacy bypass closure
nodes.norm_label: native precommit verification message postcommit handoff and truthful destination
nodes.rationale: [Contract](verification-request/CONTRACT.md) adds precommit bounded message preparation, optional current caller/email checks, postcommit VerificationSender handoff and truthful completion destinations. Concrete local HTTPS/source-wire checks cover the verification gateway trait. Public HTTP/React integration and legacy verification-writer closure remain the next enablement requirements; the full epic stays open.

nodes.label: Bounded trusted-origin message preparation before commit
nodes.community_name: Verification composition without public HTTP or legacy bypass closure
nodes.norm_label: bounded trusted-origin message preparation before commit
nodes.rationale: The message URL uses the configured base origin and /api/auth/verify-email with original token and callbackURL query parameters encoded by the URL library. Missing/empty request callback defaults to /. The existing strict origin/redirect policy is shared with recovery: secure configured origins, loopback-only HTTP development, no credentials, control characters, wildcard origins, backslash or protocol-relative escapes. Recipient/token/action URL are bounded; a message that would exceed the gateway URL budget is rejected before commit and its tentative intent rolls back. VerificationMessage owns zeroizing recipient/token/URL buffers and has no Debug/Clone/Serde, without claiming elimination of all library/parser copies.

nodes.label: Known-commit same-message verification sender handoff and uncertainty
nodes.community_name: Verification composition without public HTTP or legacy bypass closure
nodes.norm_label: known-commit same-message verification sender handoff and uncertainty
nodes.rationale: Only a known successful issuance commit releases an optional prepared message. Sender is called with no SQLite transaction held. The concrete HTTPS gateway uses the existing verification subject/wire shape and token/kind HMAC idempotency key; its bounded retries reuse identical token/payload/key. The application never automatically reissues a new token. A mail error may follow actual delivery, so it returns Committed/auth_delivery_unconfirmed and retains the original usable link. Unknown commit retires the handle and calls no sender; precommit failures roll back and require successful rollback/preflight before reuse. Injected sender ports must be bounded; sender panic or caller cancellation cannot be treated as proof that committed effects were canceled.

nodes.label: WAL/DELETE composition and actual HTTPS/source wire acceptance
nodes.community_name: Verification composition without public HTTP or legacy bypass closure
nodes.norm_label: wal/delete composition and actual https/source wire acceptance
nodes.rationale: Acceptance uses canonical synthetic control schemas and separate native processes in WAL/DELETE modes: digest visible before unlocked delivery, generic unit acknowledgement for absent/verified recipients, exact destination/default handling, invalid/oversize URL rollback, disabled sender, delivery uncertainty without reissue, current caller mismatch/expiry/revocation/workspace checks, revocation during unlocked preparation, stale link after postcommit credential change, late SQL rollback and real unknown commits for request/completion. A local HTTPS fixture exercises the actual VerificationSender implementation and compares its JSON/idempotency HMAC with the installed source sender. No external mail or real data is used. GDD readiness is structural evidence for this scoped composition only.

nodes.label: Pending public boundary coherent routing and legacy writer closure
nodes.community_name: Verification composition without public HTTP or legacy bypass closure
nodes.norm_label: pending public boundary coherent routing and legacy writer closure
nodes.rationale: Next work is the native send-verification-email/verify-email HTTP boundary, generic public response and timing/rate/caller-cookie rules, socket/source/UI checks and coherent routing that cannot fall back to the legacy verification writer. Current Rust operations are not production admission or permission to run two authoritative verification handlers. Full physical/lifetime writer and restore-lineage qualification, remaining provider/service identity, engine/client/platform/distribution parity and cutover remain required.

nodes.label: Prevalidated truthful postcommit destination without bearer injection
nodes.community_name: Verification composition without public HTTP or legacy bypass closure
nodes.norm_label: prevalidated truthful postcommit destination without bearer injection
nodes.rationale: Completion validates and constructs the successful destination before attempting the email flag mutation. It returns that destination only after known completion; omitted/empty callback yields None for a future JSON response. No verification bearer is injected into a callback, and reserved token/error/verified query coordinates are removed. Other caller-supplied path/query values and absolute URL fragments are preserved. The pure callback helper can add only fixed INVALID_TOKEN or VERIFICATION_UNCONFIRMED errors for the corresponding trusted result; unknown commits never produce the success destination. Existing one-time/current-context/flag/audit invariants remain in force, without automatic sign-in.

nodes.label: Verification composition without public HTTP or legacy bypass closure
nodes.community_name: Verification composition without public HTTP or legacy bypass closure
nodes.norm_label: verification composition without public http or legacy bypass closure
nodes.rationale: This increment composes persisted one-time verification with message preparation, an optional current caller, postcommit mail and a trusted completion destination. It does not register or enable native HTTP routes. Public acknowledgement/session-cookie parsing/timing/rate policy and closing the authoritative legacy verify-email bypass remain required before enablement. The complete Rust epic is unchanged.

nodes.label: Writer-bound optional exact current caller and bounded message preparation
nodes.community_name: Verification composition without public HTTP or legacy bypass closure
nodes.norm_label: writer-bound optional exact current caller and bounded message preparation
nodes.rationale: The request runtime receives an admitted control connection, trusted token signer/Clock/audit version, cookie verifier and RecoveryLinks origin allow-list. Connection preflight precedes disabled-sender, invalid-input or connection-reuse claims. Disabled delivery refuses before issuance. Canonical email validation, optional caller recheck and full bounded message preparation happen inside the issuance writer. Caller proof must belong to the configured cookie verifier and signer workspace; the current canonical unexpired session must still resolve to that exact email under the writer. It grants no workspace access, MFA or new session. Anonymous unknown/already-verified recipients return the same unit acknowledgement and create no intent or mail. Account existence and internal failure stages must be concealed by the future public mapper.

nodes.label: Actual-thread dedicated UID capability NoNewPrivs and umask profile
nodes.community_name: Persistent owner namespace prerequisite and required desktop profile
nodes.norm_label: actual-thread dedicated uid capability nonewprivs and umask profile
nodes.rationale: Trusted deployment supplies an absolute workspace root, exact workspace/company selection and a nonzero broker UID. The executing Linux thread must have that real/effective/saved/filesystem UID, no permitted/effective/inheritable/ambient/bounding capabilities, NoNewPrivs=1 and umask0077. Launcher/installer sets these before threads, with each operation checking /proc/thread-self/status rather than the thread-group leader; the library does not change process privileges or permissions. Root/operator and enrolled broker-UID code are trusted; normal clients and legacy tools run a different unprivileged UID. Same-UID malicious processes are not isolated by Unix file modes.

nodes.label: 41-check132-denial candidate Linux namespace proof and fake-WAL negative control
nodes.community_name: Persistent owner namespace prerequisite and required desktop profile
nodes.norm_label: 41-check132-denial candidate linux namespace proof and fake-wal negative control
nodes.rationale: Current namespace implementation is qualified by a self-contained Docker source-only driver: 41 checks, including 132 actual different-UID denials, real access/default ACL installation and read-back, same-UID/permissive positive controls, actual worker/leader NoNewPrivs divergence, prior-FD survival, WAL/DELETE lease and lock preservation, sticky retirement and explicit clean reopen. Its named volume reports the Linux ext family; a tmpfs returning EOPNOTSUPP for ACL queries is refused rather than treated as ACL-free. These candidate results do not establish disk power-loss or deployment qualification. A privileged fake-WAL negative control changes the second SQLite process to a different WAL/SHM lock protocol while raw fcntl confirms the first process's original main POSIX locks remain held. Root/operator remains trusted. Confirmed-close/BUSY quarantine, private typed host dispatch, initialization/bootstrap and all real legacy/transport flows remain unimplemented gates.

nodes.label: Required future private typed host and explicit-close quarantine discipline
nodes.community_name: Persistent owner namespace prerequisite and required desktop profile
nodes.norm_label: required future private typed host and explicit-close quarantine discipline
nodes.rationale: The forthcoming host owns private connections and uses fixed typed operations that call the existing application code. No public mutable connection callbacks/accessors or connection-bearing outputs are permitted. Bind layout before SQLite opens. Explicit close failure retains the returned connection and the entire layout/lease; retired owners accept no further work. Drop must retain/quarantine unresolved resources until process exit, rather than trusting rusqlite's best-effort destructor or releasing pinned descriptors prematurely. Construction failures and panics need the same discipline.

nodes.community_name: Persistent owner namespace prerequisite and required desktop profile

nodes.rationale: Outcome: a persistent owning runtime must acquire a protected namespace and retain it until every SQLite connection has explicitly closed. Linux dedicated UID is the first server profile; macOS local desktop remains required and is not replaced by remote-only operation. Qualification uses synthetic files only. nodes.label: Prior/inherited descriptor limitation and protected provisioning lineage
nodes.community_name: Persistent owner namespace prerequisite and required desktop profile
nodes.norm_label: prior/inherited descriptor limitation and protected provisioning lineage
nodes.rationale: File modes deny new different-UID path access. They cannot revoke a previously opened or inherited/passed descriptor. Fresh protected provisioning, no client descriptor inheritance/SCM_RIGHTS handoff and offline migration/drain are required admission conditions; no file-descriptor scan or chmod-based live takeover is claimed. Existing native reopen must retain that provisioning lineage. These conditions still need enforcement by the owning host and initializer.

nodes.label: Protected no-follow ancestry ACL sidecars and lock-preserving observation
nodes.community_name: Persistent owner namespace prerequisite and required desktop profile
nodes.norm_label: protected no-follow ancestry acl sidecars and lock-preserving observation
nodes.rationale: Walk every absolute ancestor with DIRECTORY/NOFOLLOW/CLOEXEC. Ancestors must be root- or broker-owned and not group/world writable; the workspace root and its internal directories require broker ownership and mode0700. Regular manifest/control/ledger files require broker ownership, mode0600, one link and root-device identity. Reject access/default POSIX ACL attributes or inability to establish absence. Known WAL/SHM/journal names are absent or regular single-link broker0600 files. Refuse unsafe metadata before opening regular files; no chmod/chown/unlink/repair occurs. Hold the cooperative root lease and descriptor-bound layout. Live validation uses only directory opens and statat/xattr/read_at/fstat for regular entries, never an ordinary main/sidecar/manifest inode open/close. All namespace/restore/archive/capture actions must obey the owning lifetime protocol.

Existing macOS observation tests remain valid but do not qualify this Linux deployment profile. A passing namespace slice alone is not a completed owning runtime, fresh initialization/bootstrap, HTTP/CLI/MCP composition or complete R12/epic acceptance.

nodes.label: Explicit Better Call and Better Auth fail-closed policy differences
nodes.community_name: Native current-cookie authentication increment and transitional issuance
nodes.norm_label: explicit better call and better auth fail-closed policy differences
nodes.rationale: Explicit source differences: Better Call keeps the first duplicate cookie, leniently accepts some malformed percent/quote spellings and accepts equivalent noncanonical base64 pad bits; this adapter refuses ambiguity or malformed/noncanonical wire. Legacy blank service headers count as absent, whereas this human-only adapter refuses any presented service header. Better Auth getSession permits exact expiry equality (rejects only expiresAt<now); Rentemester HTTP freshness permits exactly600000ms while Better Auth freshSessionMiddleware refuses >=600000ms. Native expiry and Fresh both use strict exclusive deadlines. The installed internalAdapter can issue24-hour dontRememberMe sessions even under expiresIn12h; native refuses lifetimes beyond12h. These are deliberate fail-closed policy differences, not claims of complete parser/session parity. Actual framework evidence uses internalAdapter session issuance and its serializer/getSession; existing actual HTTP login/MFA/reset suites remain separate regression evidence.

A real fixed synthetic key/token is allowed only in fixtures, never real secrets/company data. Native execution outside repo cwd and hostile actor/timezone environment remains deterministic for fixed Clock; SystemClock is exercised separately. Under synchronized processes, session token change/deletion is either observed before admission (deny) or blocked until ledger commit; no pre-lock token-to-ID gap or later ID-only substitution may authenticate the old token. Existing control-fence/process and access-policy suites stay green; secret/redaction, format/Clippy, scoped readiness and independent review pass. Full Rust platform completion remains unproven and active.

nodes.label: Locked exact-token lookup and trusted-clock admission
nodes.community_name: Native current-cookie authentication increment and transitional issuance
nodes.norm_label: locked exact-token lookup and trusted-clock admission
nodes.rationale: A new application entrypoint takes VerifiedCookie and a trusted runtime Clock (SystemClock in production; deterministic test implementations), not caller user/session IDs, roles, timestamps or an authenticated boolean. Authentication and freshness are admission-time checks, not commit-time validity: a later boundary crossing during company-lock acquisition or callback does not cancel already admitted synchronous work. Under control BEGIN IMMEDIATE, exact session.token lookup resolves session ID and subject; complete current control schema/history and integrity/FKs remain mandatory. Dates must be canonical UTC ISO milliseconds YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS.sssZ TEXT with valid Gregorian/time fields. Require createdAt<=now<expiresAt, positive lifetime<=the existing12-hour policy and, for Fresh operations, age<the existing10-minute freshness policy. Unknown/malformed dates, future creation, expired/deleted/retokenized sessions or stale freshness refuse before company work. Re-read the trusted clock at admission under the lock; business input cannot set it. No date coercion, session refresh/cache, renewal, cookie issuance or control data writes occur. Session IDs/subjects must be exact nonblank source text; actual current user email/MFA/access/membership and company policy still run under that same lock.

nodes.label: Native current-cookie authentication increment and transitional issuance
nodes.community_name: Native current-cookie authentication increment and transitional issuance
nodes.norm_label: native current-cookie authentication increment and transitional issuance
nodes.rationale: This R04/R13/R41 increment verifies the installed Better Auth 1.7.1 signed opaque session cookie in Rust and resolves its current database session inside the existing control-to-company fence. It does not implement login, password/MFA/recovery/reset/enrollment, service credentials, CSRF, a server endpoint or live writer admission. Better Auth issuance remains transitional; R41/R55 cannot close until complete native identity flows replace its Bun/TypeScript runtime and all migration/security gates pass. No new password or identity scheme is introduced.

nodes.label: Opaque nonserializable MAC proof with runtime-generation prerequisites
nodes.community_name: Native current-cookie authentication increment and transitional issuance
nodes.norm_label: opaque nonserializable mac proof with runtime-generation prerequisites
nodes.rationale: Only the verifier constructs VerifiedCookie; it has no Deserialize, Serialize, Debug, Clone or public constructor. Its workspace and exact bearer token can be read by trusted in-process adapters, never logged. Verification errors are fixed non-disclosing codes; key/token/signature/header values never enter diagnostics. This is proof of MAC verification under the configured key, not proof of DB identity, expiry or runtime generation. Runtime must still bind stable distinct databases, current secret/workspace generation and manifest/lifetime admission. Secure naming is not proof of TLS/origin/proxy correctness.

nodes.label: Shared fence outcomes and static permission/freshness mapping
nodes.community_name: Native current-cookie authentication increment and transitional issuance
nodes.norm_label: shared fence outcomes and static permission/freshness mapping
nodes.rationale: The existing trusted-provider entrypoint and its explicit caller obligations remain for compatibility. Both entrypoints share one transaction implementation, including WAL/DELETE admission and NotCommitted/OutcomeUnknown/Committed cleanup semantics. Cookie workspace must match the selected workspace before callback; unknown session IDs cannot be supplied through this path. Postcommit receipt replay still needs current authorization. Callback transaction-control SQL/sidechannels remain forbidden, not sandboxed. Runtime must map operation to company permission and freshness statically; callers cannot select their own required permission.

nodes.label: Strict active-key HMAC cookie wire verification
nodes.community_name: Native current-cookie authentication increment and transitional issuance
nodes.norm_label: strict active-key hmac cookie wire verification
nodes.rationale: The runtime verifier is explicitly configured with a workspace key, Secure or development cookie profile and the canonical injected active secret (unpadded base64url encoding of at least32 random bytes, as existing Rentemester config requires). HMAC uses that secret's UTF8 STRING bytes, not its decoded entropy. Better Auth's current active secrets[0].value signs/verifies session cookies; old versioned/legacy secrets are not cookie fallbacks. No environment key/default or claimed actor is consulted. Supported names are __Secure-better-auth.session_token and better-auth.session_token according to the explicit profile. Reject wrong profile, duplicate/ambiguous session cookies, missing token, malformed percent/UTF8 encoding, noncanonical44-character standard-base64 signature, invalid MAC or headers exceeding8192 bytes. Generic/cache cookies confer no authority. Optional quoted cookie syntax and percent decoding follow the emitted wire; decoded token is exact and bounded to512 bytes, nonempty and contains no control characters. Signature comparison uses maintained constant-time HMAC verification. Any presented service-key header is refused by this human-only path, including empty values; a dedicated later service adapter must handle services without cookie fallback.

nodes.label: Own-factor management with signer/profile/kind-bound session proof
nodes.community_name: Own-factor management with signer/profile/kind-bound session proof
nodes.norm_label: own-factor management with signer/profile/kind-bound session proof
nodes.rationale: Implement internal view and regenerate operations for the session's own existing enabled MFA factor. No caller user ID, email, workspace claim or raw token authorizes disclosure. Trusted runtime injects CookieVerifier/keyring/Clock/audit version and an already admitted control connection. Accept only a signed session proof bound to the same workspace, signer key and Secure/Development cookie profile; pending challenges are a separate kind and cannot substitute. This binding supplements exact current token resolution; it does not qualify physical handle/lifetime admission or legacy provider provenance.

nodes.label: Committed secret disclosure, rollback and unknown reconciliation
nodes.community_name: Own-factor management with signer/profile/kind-bound session proof
nodes.norm_label: committed secret disclosure, rollback and unknown reconciliation
nodes.rationale: Sensitive code lists retain non-Debug/non-Clone/non-Serde zeroizing owned buffers. Return codes only after known commit, including view's accepted audit. Malformed pool/key/clock/config or late SQL failure rolls back the complete operation, with no disclosure or false accepted audit; confirmed rollback determines handle reuse. Every commit error returns OutcomeUnknown, retires the handle and withholds all codes; never retry or assert rollback automatically. Lost/unknown regeneration is reconciled with another fully authenticated view or an explicit subsequent regeneration, not a blind replay. View is explicitly repeatable and is not a replay of consumed enrollment confirmation.

nodes.label: Session-selected unlocked KDF and locked exact fresh current-state recheck
nodes.community_name: Own-factor management with signer/profile/kind-bound session proof
nodes.norm_label: session-selected unlocked kdf and locked exact fresh current-state recheck
nodes.rationale: Both operations require the current password, a current session younger than ten minutes with the established twelve-hour maximum lifetime, email-verified MFA-enabled user, active workspace membership and exactly one strict verified factor. Password verification runs outside the writer lock using a canonical read snapshot selected by the verified session token. Bind the candidate subject and exact session ID, then recheck the same credential snapshot, exact current token/session ID and current fresh access/factor state under one control BEGIN IMMEDIATE. Sample trusted time at final admission; never refresh session freshness as a side effect. Account/company role escalation is not required for self management. Missing credential/provider, disabled user/access, stale/revoked/replaced session, unsupported factor state or wrong password refuses without effects. Password changes while the KDF is unlocked invalidate the operation. Existing endpoint rate/origin/blocking protection remains pending and is not claimed by this internal synchronous operation.

nodes.label: Source corrections and independent management acceptance
nodes.community_name: Own-factor management with signer/profile/kind-bound session proof
nodes.norm_label: source corrections and independent management acceptance
nodes.rationale: Acceptance uses actual canonical migrations, configured source crypto/view helper and separate native WAL/DELETE processes. Exercise source-generated and native-generated pools including consumed/empty pools; self-only fresh signed session and password; key/profile/workspace/challenge confusion; changed credential/session/access/MFA/factor state during unlocked KDF; strict expiry/freshness boundaries; old/new-code login behavior; current-pool read/replace serialization and no lost recovery consumption; late rollback and real DELETE commit-busy withholding for both operations. Preserve all previous tests. Deliberate source corrections are password/fresh-session requirements for view, exact session/credential fencing and atomic management audit. No exposed endpoint, real data, actual handle/lifetime, live dual writers, restore lineage, full identity/server/client/distribution/cutover acceptance or whole epic completion is qualified.

nodes.label: Strict zero-to-ten pool view and ten-code CAS with canonical workspace audit
nodes.community_name: Own-factor management with signer/profile/kind-bound session proof
nodes.norm_label: strict zero-to-ten pool view and ten-code cas with canonical workspace audit
nodes.rationale: View decrypts the strict existing default encrypted pool of zero through ten unique canonical case-sensitive codes. It returns the remaining pool without changing it, and appends a mfa_backup_codes_viewed event to canonical append-only workspace_audit. Audit uses entity_type native_mfa_backup_management_v1, entity_id as the canonical JSON tuple [subject,sessionId,auditKeyVersion], actor user:<subject> and created_at from sampled trusted time. Neither bearer tokens nor codes/ciphertext enter audit. Canonical auth telemetry v12 does not permit management endpoint names; no schema migration or verification-endpoint mislabel is used. Regeneration validates the old pool before replacement, generates ten fresh unique unbiased default codes and encrypts with the current configured key/fresh OS nonce. Exact old-ciphertext CAS and a mfa_backup_codes_regenerated workspace_audit event commit together. Old codes immediately cease to authenticate; the old pool, factor secret/verified flag, login failures/lock, user flags, existing sessions and TOTP replay state otherwise remain unchanged. Existing pending enrolled-login challenges bind current factor/identity and may use only the new current pool after regeneration. No setup/challenge authority, automatic session rotation or TOTP change is granted. A prior account login lock is not a shortcut to a new session and is not reset by management.

nodes.label: Non-related third party
nodes.rationale: An independent provider qualifies; the owner’s home NAS does not.

nodes.label: Weekly full backup
nodes.rationale: Documented BEK205 §4 requires transactions and documents at least weekly unless unchanged; manifest timestamps/hashes encode cadence.

nodes.label: Human-attested compliance guides
nodes.rationale: The program cannot know cloud location, SaaS plan or provider datacenter changes.

nodes.label: Deterministic compliance report
nodes.rationale: Same ledger and as-of inputs produce identical HTML; SHA-256 lets an auditor detect modifications.

nodes.label: Rule-to-provision mapping
nodes.rationale: Report groups rule IDs by category with legal citations.

nodes.label: Rule documentation synchronization
nodes.rationale: Rule YAML, enforcement point, both matrices and human guides must change together; new sources require legal registry/scope updates.

nodes.label: Law → rule → implementation → human guide
nodes.rationale: Bidirectional traceability exposes both legal origins and requirements for a system area.

nodes.label: DK-BOOKKEEPING-BACKUP-001
nodes.rationale: Hybrid weekly full backup of posted transactions/documents with timestamp/hash manifest.

nodes.label: Exact deterministic accrual allocation
nodes.rationale: Balanced parking entry apportioned across periods; final-period penny remainder preserves exact sum.

nodes.label: Locked-year class-B report and advisory tax basis
nodes.norm_label: locked-year class-b report and advisory tax basis
nodes.rationale: Complete master data and locked year produce limited-taxonomy iXBRL; uncertain tax adjustments need review; filing external.

nodes.label: Human-confirmed immediate asset writeoff
nodes.rationale: Linear depreciation preserves purchase links; immediate writeoff needs user decision and source-backed threshold.

nodes.label: Period-bound authority and SAF-T export
nodes.rationale: Deterministic machine-readable package uses manifest hashes and declares unsupported sections.

nodes.label: Verified restore and human backup governance
nodes.norm_label: verified restore and human backup governance
nodes.rationale: Weekly transaction/document backup, independent EU/EEA destination; manifest/hash verified before readable restore.

nodes.label: Lossless bank import and reconciliation
nodes.rationale: Original batch data and FX retained; running balance continuity is warning; matched/unmatched records exposed.

nodes.label: Idempotent append-only SMTP delivery log
nodes.rationale: Send records append-only; encrypted SMTP credentials are practice rather than standalone rule ID.

nodes.label: Content-addressed immutable documents
nodes.rationale: SHA256 and immutable originals preserve evidence while statutory exception receipts retain original/currency.

nodes.label: Mail intake deduplication and human exception queue
nodes.norm_label: mail intake deduplication and human exception queue
nodes.rationale: Message-id plus attachment hash deduplicates; ambiguity needs human resolution.

nodes.label: Validated immutable sequential invoice issuance
nodes.rationale: Fields/arithmetic/master-data are validated before issuance; numbered issued snapshots cannot change.

nodes.label: Append-only balanced journal
nodes.rationale: Entries balance, require relevant documents and corrections use traceable reversal instead of mutation.

nodes.label: Deterministic single-registration late-payment claims
nodes.rationale: Interest, reminder limits/spacing and fixed B2B compensation register and book only once.

nodes.label: Closed-period and future-date guards
nodes.rationale: Reject journal entries in closed accounting periods or future dates.

nodes.label: Append-only master data and historical snapshots
nodes.norm_label: append-only master data and historical snapshots
nodes.rationale: Resolve/materialize fields before issuance/intake so later customer/vendor changes cannot alter old evidence.

nodes.label: Public OIOUBL/PEPPOL handoff and idempotent submission
nodes.norm_label: public oioubl/peppol handoff and idempotent submission
nodes.rationale: Immutable EAN buyer snapshot and deterministic export; access point/certificate setup remains external human work.

nodes.label: Prevalidated recurring invoice template
nodes.rationale: Immutable specification has legal content basis; deterministic generation rule has no legal source.

nodes.label: Five-year retention bounds GDPR erasure
nodes.rationale: Fiscal-year end plus five years controls erase rejection and append-only tombstones; subject export remains available.

nodes.label: Traceable invoice settlement and corrections
nodes.rationale: Payments, credit notes, refunds and bad-debt writeoffs preserve invoice and bank linkage.

nodes.label: Code/hybrid/human enforcement classification
nodes.rationale: Separates machine-checkable invariants from human assertions rather than pretending code knows external facts.

nodes.label: DK-BOOKKEEPING-BACKUP-DEST-001
nodes.rationale: Human-signed three-condition destination assertion documented as a rule; differs from older master-guide wording.

nodes.label: GDPR-RETENTION-BOUNDED-ERASURE
nodes.rationale: Retention deadline determines lawful erase and rejection tombstones.

nodes.label: Internal agent/import/generation integrity rules
nodes.rationale: Runtime permissions, migration reconciliation and recurring generation have no direct law source.

nodes.label: Legal source IDs and scope registry
nodes.norm_label: legal source ids and scope registry
nodes.rationale: Machine registry plus scoped provisions feed regulatory coverage; source law dates are recorded citations, not freshly verified current law.

nodes.label: Legal rule enforcement matrix
nodes.rationale: Documents the nonregistered baseline; each obligation mapped to YAML, enforcement and human guide.

nodes.label: DK-BOOKKEEPING-RESTORE-001
nodes.rationale: Manifest and hashes verified before restoring readable dataset.

nodes.label: DK-BOOKKEEPING-RETENTION-001
nodes.rationale: retain_until = financial year end plus five years.

nodes.label: DK-BOOKKEEPING-BACKUP-KEY-ROTATE-001
nodes.rationale: Rotation must remain auditable and preserve verification of older backups.

nodes.label: hard_stop / warning / advisory severity
nodes.rationale: Blocking, report-only and best-practice levels have distinct operational meanings.

nodes.label: Provision text_hash maintenance
nodes.rationale: Rules bind provision references and hashes; matrix maintained manually in same change.

nodes.label: BEK302/2025 documented repeal of BEK1383 §2(2)-(3)
nodes.rationale: Recorded amendment effective 2026-01-01; verified 2026-05-24 by Mikkel Krogsholm, not a live law check.

nodes.label: Recorded financial-subsidiary exemption repeal
nodes.rationale: The recorded repeal removes group-accounting exemption; described outside target segment.

nodes.label: Hypothetical financial-subsidiary backup reassessment
nodes.rationale: Future service to financial subsidiaries would require revisiting backup exemption; explicitly not active duty.

nodes.label: Recorded exhausted implementation dates
nodes.rationale: Recorded 2024-07-01 / 2025-01-01 phase-in provisions removed after exhaustion.

nodes.label: Legal amendment verification workflow
nodes.rationale: Register source/XML, read exact operative changes, match cited provisions and update hashes/matrix if affected.

nodes.label: Recorded unaffected §1-based rules
nodes.rationale: Log says storage/cash/foreign/intake/vendor rules cite untouched §1, so no rule ID/text_hash update required.

nodes.label: Proposed internal-to-standard chart mapping
nodes.description: A slim posting chart maps to official accounts, annual report lines and XBRL concepts.
nodes.rationale: Separate daily posting ergonomics from official export/reporting classifications.

nodes.label: Builder agent production-data isolation
nodes.description: Builder modifies repository code, tests and migrations but must not access production ledger, mail or SMTP.

nodes.label: Proposed fail-closed exception queue
nodes.description: Certain work posts; uncertain work blocks or creates an exception with required human context.
nodes.rationale: A system must post correctly or refuse rather than rely on model guesses.

nodes.label: Proposed negative golden accounting cases
nodes.description: Missing VAT amount and missing restaurant purpose fixtures assert rejection/blocking tied to rules.

nodes.label: Original staged source-of-truth maturity vision
nodes.description: Original v0.x/v1.0 milestones and hypothetical MCP command names are plans, not current CLI contracts; core stability precedes broader reporting.

nodes.label: Proposed preserved document and mail evidence
nodes.description: Raw mail, attachments and metadata/hashes remain evidence; replacing a document preserves old versions.
nodes.norm_label: proposed preserved document and mail evidence

nodes.label: Rule maintainer reviewed source updates
nodes.description: Rule maintainer observes official sources and proposes rule/test PRs; it cannot deploy unreviewed rules.

nodes.label: Proposed machine rules and legal source provenance
nodes.description: Rules reference versioned downloaded official sources, hashes and provisions; explanatory skills are separate from enforcement.
nodes.norm_label: proposed machine rules and legal source provenance

nodes.label: Runtime bookkeeper least privilege
nodes.description: Runtime agent reads evidence and posts through approved interfaces; it may not change production code or rules.

nodes.label: Proposed immutable invoice lifecycle
nodes.description: Validate, issue sequential number, PDF, transport log, book sale and later settle bank; issued mistakes use credit notes and new invoices.

nodes.label: Proposed deterministic accounting core
nodes.description: Vision layers controlled CLI/MCP over append-only SQLite, validators, rules, hashes and evidence; sample schemas are proposals.

nodes.label: Proposed separation of agent duties
nodes.description: Vision specification defines runtime bookkeeper, builder and rule maintainer as separate roles; it is design intent rather than an implementation inventory.
